parties:
Khurshid Alam (Md) ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Judge, Artha Rin Adalat-1 ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Mirza Hussain Haider J: This Rule Nisi has been issued calling upon the respondents "to show cause as to why the continuation of the proceeding of Artha Rin Execution Case No. 1176 of 2003 pending before the Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Chittagong, filed allegedly beyond the statutory period of twelve (12) years, shall not he declared to be without lawful authority and is of no legal effect".

2. Facts stated in the writ petition, in short, are that the respondent No. 2 bank, filed Money Suit No. 158 of 1986 in the First Commercial Court and Subordinate Judge, Chittagong, for recovery of loan from the petitioner. The suit was decreed ex parte on 2-1-1991. Thereafter, the respondent bank filed Money Execution Case No. 49 of 1992 for execution of the decree. The said execution case was pending till 16-5-2003. But ultimately the same was dismissed for default by order dated 16-5-2003. Thereafter, on 13-11-2003 the bank filed another execution case, bearing Artha Rin Execution Case No. 1176 of 2003 (which has been challenged herein) in the Court of respondent No. 1. It is alleged by the petitioner in the writ petition that the bank filed the instant execution case long after 12 years 10 months from the date of decree. It is further stated that the executing court, on receipt of the instant execution case, fixed a date for hearing on acceptability of the same on the ground that the same has been filed after 12 years from the date of decree. The Court by its order No. 9 dated 22-3-2004 held that since the previous execution case has been dismissed for default on 16-5-2003 subsequent filing of the execution case on 13-11-2003 is very much within time and, as such, there is no bar in holding that the instant execution case has been filed in accordance with law. Subsequently, the notice of the .execution case was issued and 8-8-2004 was fixed for auction sale of the petitioner's mortgaged property. The petition on 1-8-2004 appeared in the instant execution case and filed application under section 57 of the Ain 2003 alleging that the instant execution case is barred by limitation and, as such, the same is liable to be rejected in liming. The petitioner also prayed for stay of the proposed auction sale to be held on 8-8-2004. The executing court fixed 4-8-2004 for filing objection by the bank against the said prayer and for hearing of the same. On 4-8-2004 the decree holder bank appeared and filed objection against the said prayer and on hearing both the parties, the Adalat by its order No. 18 dated 4-8-2004 held that the filing of the instant execution case being within 1 year from the date of dismissal of the earlier execution case on 16-5-2003, the instant-execution case is not barred by limitation. Moreover, the decree being not challenged in higher court and there being no order of stay of the execution case by any higher authority the judgment debtor cannot pray for staying the proceeding of the execution case nor can raise any objection to the same. As such, the prayer for dismissing the execution case was rejected and the execution case was directed to proceed in accordance with law. Thereafter, the petitioner prayed for stay of the proceeding of the execution case subject to obtaining stay order from the High Court Division. The said prayer was also rejected by the Adalat on the ground that section 31 of the Ain 2003 prohibits such prayer unless there is a specific order from the higher court. However, the execution case continued.

3. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the rejection of the aforesaid prayers made by the petitioner the instant Rule Nisi has been obtained by the petitioner in the terms as stated hereinabove.

4. The respondent bank entered appearance in this Rule and filed affidavit-in-opposition denying the material allegations made in the writ petition. It is contended that the Execution Case No. 49 of 1992 being dismissed for default on 16-5-2003 the bank on 13-11-2003 filed the instant execution case which is very much permissible under section 28(3) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003 by which the previous Ain 1990 has been repealed.

5. Mr Md Naseruddin Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, referring to Annexure-A (i.e. the application for execution of the decree) submits that it is evident that Money Suit No. 158 of 1986 was filed and the suit was decreed on 2-1-1991. Thereafter, Money Execution Case No. 49 of 1992 was filed earlier, in the Commercial Court, which was subsequently dismissed for default on 16-5-2003. He again submits that the said execution case was never transferred from the Commercial Court to the Artha Rin Adalat, which is evident from the number of the execution case itself. According to him, had the execution case been transferred to the Artha Rin Adalat, the same would have been renumbered as Artha Rin Execution Case No. 49 of 1992 in place of Money Execution Case No. 49 of 1992. As such, the same continued before the Commercial Court and was dismissed by the said Commercial Court. Thus, he submits that the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003 does not permit filing of any execution case before such Adalat which did not continue after the Artha Rin Adalat constituted under the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 1990. So the execution case being not dismissed for default by Artha Rin Adalat, constituted under the Ain of 1990, filing of a fresh execution case under section 28(3) of the Ain 2003 is illegal. The filing of second execution case is admittedly beyond 12 years from the decree and, as such, the same cannot be allowed to proceed with under the law of 2003. 'Referring to section 28 of the Ain 2003, he submits that any decree put into execution after 180 days from the date of decree, the same is barred by limitation and such execution case shall not be accepted rather be rejected. Referring to section 28(3) of the Ain 2003, he further submits that the earlier execution case being not filed or proceeded with before the Artha Rin Adalat, the filing of the subsequent case within 1 year from the date of dismissal, as provided under section 28(3) of the Ain, cannot be invoked by the decree holder bank. Again, referring section 28(4), he submits, that since no execution case was filed before the Artha Rin Adalat and since 12 years have already passed from the date of decree the filing of the new execution case after 6 years from the date of filing of the earlier one is also barred by limitation and, as such, the instant execution case is liable to be rejected. Lastly, Mr Chowdhury submits that even if the execution case can proceed under the present Ain, the proceeding of the same is barred for non completion of the same within 90 days or within 150 days as provided in section 37 of the Ain 2003 and, as such, the proceeding of the Execution Case No. 1176 of 2003 is liable to be declared illegal. In support of his contention, he relied on the case of Montaj Ali Akonda and others vs Kefatullah Mondal being dead his heirs 1(a) son A Hamid and others reported in 7 MLR (AD) 138 and on the case of Bangladesh Jatiya Samabaya Bank Ltd vs Sang bad Daily Paper and others reported in 36 DLR (AD) 5.

6. On the other hand, Mr Khalilur Rahman Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent bank, submits that the petitioner has not taken the plea in his writ petition that the earlier execution case was not transferred to the Court of Artha Rin Adalat constituted under Ain, 1990 nor raised any question as to renumbering the same under the said law, as such, this being a question of fact he cannot take this plea before this Hon'ble Court at this stage for the purpose of disposal of the Rule. He next submits that section 9 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 1990 categorically says that every suit, concerning realization of loan by the financial institution, pending in any court for disposal, the same will be transferred to the Artha Rin Adalat constituted under Artha Rin Adalat Ain 1990 and will be proceeded with by the said Adalat in accordance with law from the date of effect of the said law of 1990. Therefore, the decree being passed in 1991 and the earlier execution case being filed in 1992 it can be presumed, considering the provision of law, that the said decree has been passed by the Artha Rin Adalat and the execution case has also been filed before the Artha Rin Adalat which was in existence on that date. Thus he submits that from the materials on record, it is evident that the suit being decreed in 1991 by the. Artha Rin Adalat constituted under Artha Rin Adalat Ain 1990 and accordingly, the earlier execution case being filed in 1992 the same was filed before the Adalat constituted under the Ain 1990. In the meantime on 1-5-2003, the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003 having come into effect the said execution case was transferred to the Adalat constituted under section 60(3) of the new Ain of 2003. Accordingly, he submits that the earlier execution case being dismissed for default on 16-5-2003, section 28(3) of the Ain, 2003 empowered the decree holder bank to file subsequent execution case within one year from the date of dismissal or disposal of the earlier execution case and, as such, the instant execution case being filed on 13-11-2003, the filing of the same is very much within 1 year from the date of disposal of the earlier case by the Artha Rin Adalat. Hence, there is no illegality in proceeding with the said execution case.

7. Heard the learned Advocates and perused the writ petition along with all the annexure appended thereto. It appears from the writ petition as well as from the annexure that the petitioner did not make any assertion as to the transfer of the execution case to the Artha Rin Adalat nor he made any statement in the writ petition itself in support of his claim. The petitioner also did not make or include any reliable or relevant statement supported by sufficient material in support of his contentions nor his contentions, as to what he submitted, is supported by sufficient documents. Since it is the duty of the petitioner to prove his own case and since in the case of Mustafa Kamal and another vs Commissioner of Customs and others, reported in 52 DLR (AD) 1 it has been held initially, in the writ petition itself the writ petitioner must include some reliable and relevant materials in support of his claim'; we cannot accept the submissions of the petitioner as to the case was not transferred to the Artha Rin Adalat and the same was not dismissed by the Artha Rin Adalat. The only material placed before us, wherefrom we can gather that the earlier execution case was dismissed, is Annexure "A", the present application for execution of decree filed on 13-11-2003 under Order XXI, rule 11 of the Code. In the said application under the 1st column it appears Commercial Sub-Judge Court, Chittagong Money Suit No. 158 of 1986" has been inserted. Under the third column the date of the decree has been shown as 21-1-1991 and thereafter in column 6 under the heading 'previous application, if any, with date and result', it has been mentioned that Money Execution Case No. 49 of 1992 has been dismissed for default on 16-5-2003. From the above it is clear that decree was passed in January 1991 and the execution case was filed in 1992. On the other hand, it appears that the said Artha Rin Adalat Ain 1990 was promulgated on 28-10-1990 and by section 11 of the said Ain the Artha Rin Adalat Ordinance 16 of 1989 was repealed. So, it is clear that the Ain of 1990, through its earlier Ordinance being No. 16 of 1989, came into effect from 1989 and all cases pending before the then Commercial Courts were transferred by operation of law to the Artha Rin Adalats constituted under section 4 of the Act IV of 1990. This was done by amending section 9 of Ain 1990 vide Act No. 51 of 1990.

<u>8. However, from the above circumstances it appears that the decree passed in 1991 is a decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat and for execution of the said decree the execution case filed in 1992 was also filed before the Artha Rin Adalat since there was no suit of the Financial Institutions pending before any Commercial Court after 1990. Thereafter, Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003 having come into force on 1-5-2003 upon repealing the Ain of 1990, the said execution case was transferred to the Artha Rin Adalat constituted under the Ain 2003 pursuant to section 60(3) of the said Ain. As such, dismissal of the said execution case on 16-5-2003 for default was made by the Adalat constituted under Ain 2003. Hence, filing of the second execution case on 13-11-2003 is very much within one year of the dismissal of the earlier case and is wholly within the scope of section 28(3) of the said Ain of 2003. Thus, there is no illegality in filing of the execution case and continuation of the proceeding of the same.</u>

<u>9. Relying on the decision of 52 DLR as referred above, we are of the view that the petitioner did not come with bold assertion and did not include any relevant material to show that the execution case was not transferred to the Artha Rin Adalat. Under such circumstances, it can be held that the earlier execution case being dismissed by the Artha Rin Adalat after the new Ain of 2003 came into force, the filing of the subsequent execution case No. 1176 of 2003 on 13-11-2003 is very much within 1 year from the date of disposal of the earlier execution case and, as such, the filing and continuation of the proceedings of the said execution case is very much within the scope of law.</u>

<u>10. However, since in the instant execution case it has been filed within one year from the date of disposal of the earlier case the filing of the instant execution case is very much within the purview of the law and, as such, there is nothing to interfere with the same in this Rule. The observations made by the Adalat in this respect appears to be correct and we do not find any reason for interference with the same. Moreover, the time limit fixed by section 37 of the Ain 2003, for disposal of execution case within 150 days being "directory" not "mandatory", as decided in Writ Petition No. 7615 of 2005 (M Serajul Islam vs Bangladesh) by this bench, there is no illegality in the proceedings of the execution case. The proceeding continuing before the Artha Rin Adalat being in accordance with law there is no legal flaw in the same.</u>

11. Considering the facts and circumstances as stated hereinabove, we do not find any merit in the Rule and hence, the Rule is liable to be discharged.

Accordingly, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.778 of 1997.
lawyer:
N H Khandker, Advocate-on-Record — For the Petitioner. 
Not represented—The Respondents.
parties:
Hazrat Ali Matbar Wakf Estate ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Government of Bangladesh represented by the Deputy Commissioner & ors ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 25 May 1997 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2664 of 1996)
full_judgment:
Bimalendu Bikash Roy Chowdhury J: Leave to appeal has been sought by the plaintiff against the order of remand dated 25 May 1977 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.2654 of 1996 which arose out of a suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession in respect of 1.05 acre of land comprised within SA Plot Nos.2086 and 2087 of Mouza Singair filed before a Subordinate Judge, Manikganj.

2. Briefly, the facts, as narrated by the plaintiff are that the suit land on which hat is situate appertained to the wakf estate created by its original owner Hazrat Ali Matbar. The hat originally situated elsewhere in the village and after diluvia of the land on which the hat was situate was shifted to the suit land and so it was not subject to acquisition under the provisions of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The plaintiff also obtained decree on compromise against the Government who has taken over the property as being non retainable under sub-section (2A) of section 20 of the said Act.

3. The defence contention of the Government and its officers (defendants) is that the hat in question belonged to Nagendra Lal Shaha and others and that it was acquired by the Government in accordance with the provisions of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act on payment of compensation.

<u>4. The trial Court decreed the suit. The appellate Court reversed the decision. The High Court Division in revision sent back the case on remand to the trial Court for trial afresh after framing fresh issues in the light of certain observations made by it. The said court also afforded a chance to the plaintiff to amend the plaint and the defendants to file additional written statement, if any, leaving the parties to adduce further evidence, both oral and documentary, if so advised.</u>

<u>5. The High Court Division pointed out, amongst other things, that there was nothing on record about the date on which the hat began its sitting upon the suit land and whether the wakf state was a rent receiver. There was also omission of the discussion of law necessary for proper decision.</u>

<u>6. It may be observed that there are a number of other aspects of the case not considered by any of the courts below. But since it is an open remand and the plaintiff-petitioner has not been prejudiced we are not inclined to interfere.</u>

The petition is dismissed.

End.

lawyer:
Md Amir Hossain, Advocate-on-Record— For Respondent No. 1 
Not represented— Respondent No. 10.
parties:
Abdul Hai and others ------ Appellants
Vs.
Atar Islam and others ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 15-2-1999 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3023 of 1994)
full_judgment:
MM Ruhul Amin J : This appeal by leave is directed against the judgment and order dated 15-2-1999 passed by a single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3023 of 1994 making the Rule absolute and thereby setting aside the judgment and order dated 16-8-1984 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 4th Court, Comilla in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 85 of 1992 reversing the judgment and order dated 24-5-1992 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Comilla Sadar, in Miscellaneous Case No. 35 of 1990.

2. Short fact are that, the plaintiff-respondent filed Title Suit No 263 of 1986 for declaration of title and confirmation of possession and for permanent injunction on the assertions made in the plaint. The predecessor of the defendant petitioner filed written statement. The suit was fixed on 23-10-1989 for ex parte hearing. On that date the defendant did not appear and take any step. Accordingly, the suit was decreed ex parte. The defendant filed Miscellaneous Case No. 35 of 1990 under Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the ex parte decree stating, inter alia, that, he was an old man and was suffering from various ailments and he relied upon the clerk of his engaged Advocate for making tadbir in the case. His further case was that, he was not aware of the ex parte decree in question. The plaintiff-opposite party filed written objection in the abovementioned miscellaneous case denying the contentions of the defendant petitioner. The learned Assistant Judge after hearing the parties dismissed the case holding that the defendant was not prevented by sufficient cause from appearing when the case was called on for hearing. The defendant took an appeal to the Court of District Judge, Comilla, The appeal was allowed and the judgment and order passed by the trial Court was set aside. Thereafter, the plaintiff filed Civil Revision No. 3023 of 1994 against the judgment and order passed by the appellate Court and obtained a Rule. The High Court Division by judgment and order dated 15-2-1999 made the Rule absolute after setting aside the judgment and order of the appellate Court on the findings that the appellate Court did not controvert the findings of facts arrived at by the trial Court and thereby committed serious error in law which prejudiced the plaintiff.

3. Leave was granted to consider the submissions that the appellate Court correctly held that 3 tax receipts alleged to have been granted by the plaintiff opposite party respondents intending to prove that the defendant petitioner was not sick, were not proved in evidence and that the contention of the petitioners that clerk Ibrahim of the engaged Advocate of the defendant petitioner did not inform him the date of hearing of the case and the defendant was vigilant and there was no laches on his part to pursue the matter in that he was thoroughly present in the Court but on the date of hearing owing to his illness, could not appear before the Court, but the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division without adverting to the findings of the court of appeal set aside the judgment of Court of appeal and, as such, the judgment of the High Court Division is not a proper judgment of reversal and hence cannot be maintained in law and that the High Court Division failed to notice that the trial Court passed the decision on conjecture and surmise and inadmissible evidence relating to 3 tax receipts.

4. We have heard Mr Md Amir Hossain, learned Counsel for the appellants and Mr Mahbubey Alam, the learned Senior Counsel for respondent No. 19 and perused the connected papers.

5. It is on record that Other Class Suit No. 263 of 1986 brought by the respondent was decreed ex parte on 23-10-1989 and Miscellaneous Case No. 35 of 1990 under Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure was brought by Abdul Hamid, predecessor-in-interest of the petitioners for setting aside the ex parte decree on the grounds, inter alia, that he engaged one Ibrahim, clerk of his engaged Advocate, to make tadbir in the case and the clerk assured him that he was not required to go to the Court on all dates and when necessary he would inform the petitioner of the case accordingly, The clerk of the learned Advocate did not contact the petitioner for 23 months and accordingly, the petitioner went to Comilla town and learnt that Ibrahim left the profession. The petitioner on 5-5-1990 learned that the suit was decreed ex parte on 23-8-1989. The further case of the petitioner was that he was sick at the relevant time and, as such, could not appear and contest the suit. It appears that the trial Court disbelieved the petitioner's case altogether as the petitioner did not examine any witness in support of his illness and also in support of the case that one Ibrahim clerk of the engaged Advocate was entrusted with the whole matter and the Advocate's clerk did not inform anything regarding the case. The trial Court held that three tax receipts dated 21-10-1989, 31-5-1989 and 24-11-1989 Exhibit A-series were filed by the plaintiff to show that at the relevant time the defendant petitioner collected taxes by going to the villages and, as such, he was not sick. The trial Court also held that defendant petitioner did not adduce any evidence to prove his other contentions made in the case under Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The trial Court of appeal, on the other hand, allowed the appeal holding that the tax receipts Exhibit A-series were not proved in evidence according to law and the party concerned should not suffer for the default of his engaged Advocate's clerk. Even if the tax receipts are left out of consideration, then also the case of the defendant petitioner was not proved as he did not adduce any evidence in support of his case.

6. It appears that there was delay of 6 months 7 days in filing the miscellaneous case under Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the causes of delay were not at all satisfactorily explained. Accordingly, the High Court Division made the Rule absolute holding that the appellate Court did not consider the matter in its proper perspective and allowed miscellaneous case without any evidence at all and on mere surmise and conjecture.

<u>7. Thus, it is clear that the findings of the High Court Division that the petitioner could not prove that he was prevented by sufficient cause from appearing when the suit was taken up for hearing and decreed ex parte are based on correct assessment of the materials on record.</u>

8. The learned Advocate for the appellant could not point out any legal infirmity in the judgment of the High Court Division.

The appeal is accordingly dismissed without any order as to costs.

End.

parties:
Jahanara Begum being dead her heirs Sheikh Shahnaz Begum and others ------ Appellants
Vs.
Hazera Khatun being dead her heirs Md Aminul Haque & ors ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 22 November 2000 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1967 of 1999).
full_judgment:
Md Fazlul Karim J: These appeals by leave are directed against the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1967 of 1999.

2. The facts relevant for disposal of these appeals are the appellant in Civil Appeal No. 438 of 2001 as the plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 27 of 1976 in the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for specific performance of contract against the present respondent No. 8 who allegedly entered into a contract for sale of the suit property on 12-9-1979 receiving an earnest money of Taka 30,000 out of a total consideration of Taka 1,50,000 and when respondent No. 8 tried to avoid execution and registration of the sale deed the appellants had to file the aforesaid suit.

3. The appellant in Civil Appeal No. 439 of 2001 was defendant No. 3 in the suit who filed the written statement stating, inter alia, that while he was a monthly tenant in part of the suit premises the original owner respondent No. 8 entered into a written agreement with him for the sale of the premises on 21-4-1968 and received a sum of Taka 1,50,000 out of Taka 3,50,000. His further case is that in Title Suit No. 53 of 1973 he got a decree of permanent injunction. "

4. Respondent No. 8, the original owner of the suit property by filing a written statement denied the contract with the appellants stating that the alleged Bainapatra dated 12-9-1970 is false, ante-dated and fraudulently created.

5. Title Suit No. 27 of 1976 was decreed ex parte on 5-1-1985 and the Kabala was executed and registered through the Court. The respondent Nos. 1-6, however, purchased the suit land from the plaintiff Jahanara Begum but meanwhile respondent No. 7, the appellant in Civil Appeal No. 439 of 2001, filed Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1996 under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure and upon contested hearing Miscellaneous Case was allowed setting aside the said ex parte decree. The said appellant on 5-4-1998 filed an application before the trial Court under Order VI, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure for amendment of the written statement by inserting two paragraphs therein and upon hearing the parties the trial Court allowed the said prayer by order dated 27-5-1999. The appellant in Civil Appeal No. 439 of 2001 moved the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1967 of 1999 against the said impugned order dated 27-5-1999 whereupon the Rule was issued with an ad-interim order of stay of all further proceedings of the said Title Suit. The said appellant, however, in order to get the suit disposed of expeditiously instructed to get the Rule discharged for non-prosecution and accordingly, filed an application on 14-11-2000 praying for discharging the Rule for non-prosecution. The respondent Nos. 1-6 who were third party to the suit filed an application before the High Court Division praying for adding them to be the defendants in Title Suit No. 27 of 1976 and opposite parties in Civil Revision claiming that their predecessor-in-interest Hazera Khatun entered into an agreement for sale with said Jahanara Begum on 11-11-1995 and therefore, they are necessary parties in the suit as well as in the civil revision and both the petitions came up for hearing on 22-11-2000 before the High Court Division but the application of the appellant for discharging the Rule was rejected as the same was not accompanied by any affidavit in support of the application. Thereafter both the appellants Jahanara Begum and Kazi Ashrafuddin Ahmed filed an application for discharging the Rule for non-prosecution so that the original suit may be disposed of early and upon hearing, the same was rejected by the High Court Division while allowing an application of the respondent Nos. 1-6 filed in the High Court Division for transposing them as the petitioners in the Civil Revision alleging that they will suffer irreparable loss and injury if the Rule was discharged for non-prosecution. The High Court Division after hearing the parties struck out the names of the appellants from the civil revision and transposed the respondent Nos. 1-6 as the petitioners in their place.

6. Thereafter, the appellants filed the petition for leave to appeal against the said impugned order whereupon the leave was granted to consider the submission of the learned Counsel for the appellants that the High Court Division committed grave illegality in striking out the names of the petitioners of civil revision and transposing the respondents as the petitioners who are not parties to the suit itself nor assignees in the same and allowing them to proceed with the revisional application. It also submitted that the High Court Division failed to consider that a person who is not a party in the suit is not entitled to file such an application as a stranger cannot be allowed to proceed with such a revisional application. It is also submitted that respondents being not parties to the suit and the Rule having arisen out of an order passed by the Subordinate Judge allowing the prayer for amendment of the written statement, they do not have any locus standi to contest the impugned order and, in that view of the matter, the learned Judges of the High Court Division fell into an error in transposing them as the petitioners striking out the names of the original petitioners who are none else than the plaintiffs and, as such, the impugned order is not sustainable in law. It is also submitted that the High Court Division totally misconceived the provision of law as regards transposition of the parties and in the facts and circumstances of the instant case, particularly when the added respondents claimed that the plaintiff-appellants entered into a contract with them for selling the suit property after the suit was decreed on 5-1-85 as the so-called contract has nothing to do with the subject matter of the present suit. It is submitted that when the plaintiff-appellants prayed for discharging the Rule for non-prosecution third party-respondents having no interest in the suit property cannot be allowed to proceed with the revisional application and the learned Judge of the High Court Division erred in law in striking out the names of the plaintiff-appellants from the rule petition upon rejecting their prayer for discharging the Rule for non-prosecution, instead in their place transposing the strangers to the suit.

7. Mr TH Khan, the learned Counsel appearing for the appellants in Civil Appeal No. 438 of 2001 and Mr Mahbubey Alam, the learned Counsel appearing for the appellants in Civil Appeal No. 439 of 2001 have submitted that the High Court Division acted illegally in striking out the names of the rule petitioners namely, Jahanara Begum and Sheikh Shahnaz Begum, the appellants while transposing the respondent Nos. 1-6, the third parties, who were not parties to the suit and were not entitled to file such application as a stranger cannot be allowed to proceed with the revisional application against the order passed by the Subordinate Judge allowing the prayer for amendment of the written statement filed by the appellants in Civil Appeal No. 439 of 2001 as they had no locus standi to contest the said order inasmuch as the High Court Division totally misconceived the provision of law as regards the transposition of the parties in the facts and circumstance of the case, particularly when the added respondent claimed that the plaintiff-appellants entered into an agreement with them for sale after the suit was decreed as the so-called contract has nothing to do with the subject matter of the present suit inasmuch as the said ex parte decree on the basis of which the added respondents entered into an agreement with plaintiff of the suit was set aside and the suit was restored to its original file and number allowing the parties to the suit to proceed with the same in accordance with the law. The learned Counsels have further submitted that when the third party respondents have not acquired any interest to the suit land they could not be allowed to proceed with the revisional application striking out the names of the original petitioner, plaintiff-appellant and in its place transposing the name of the respondents Nos. 1-6 who were admittedly no parties to the suit.

8. Mr Md Fazlul Karim, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondents in both the appeals, has however submitted that respondent Nos. 1-6, having entered into an agreement dated 11-11-95 to purchase the suit land with the appellant Jahanara Begum pursuant to an ex parte decree, could always be impleaded as the defendant or the co-plaintiffs where it is necessary for a complete adjudication upon the question involved in the suit and to avoid multiplicity of the proceeding under the provision of Order I, rule 10(b) of the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned Counsel has further submitted that the withdrawal of the civil revision and discharge of the Rule for non-prosecution against an order allowing amendment to the written statement by the appellant in Civil Appeal No. 439 of 2001 smack of foul play on the part of Jahanara Begum, the plaintiff-appellant and others in Civil Appeal No. 438 of 2001 of an unholy alliance of non-prosecution with the suit to the prejudice of the interest of the respondent Nos. 1-6.

9. Admittedly, the suit has been filed by the appellant Jahanara Begum and others for specific performance of contract in respect of an agreement for sale dated 12-9-79 against respondent No. 8 on receipt of Taka 30,000 out of total consideration of Taka 1,50,000 and respondent No. 7, who was impleaded in the suit is the monthly tenant in the part of the suit land under the owner respondent No. 8, has allegedly entered into an agreement for sale of part of the suit land on the basis of an agreement dated 21-4-1968. The said respondent No. 7 filed Title Suit No. 53 of 1973 which was decreed and pursuant to which obtained kabala executed and registered through Court. The said respondent No. 7, the appellant in Civil Appeal No. 439 of 2001 has entered appearance in the suit and filed written statement. It appears that after lapse of considerable period of time the respondent No. 7 filed an application for amendment of the written statement which was allowed by order dated 27-5-1999 against which the appellant and others filed revisional application in the High Court Division upon which a Rule being Civil Revision No. 1967 of 1999 was issued together with ad-interim order of stay of all further proceedings of the suit. It appears that the said appellant filed an application on 14-11-2000 praying for discharge of the Rule for non-prosecution to enable them for early disposal of the suit and in the Rule the present respondent Nos. 1-6 as the third parties filed an application before the High Court Division for transposition of the opposite party in the civil revision claiming that their predecessor entered into an agreement for sale with jahanara Begum and, as such, they are the necessary parties in the suit as well as in the civil revision and for transposing their names as the petitioners in the Rule application while striking out the names of the petitioner in the civil revision. The same having been allowed the appellants moved this Court and leave as aforesaid was accordingly granted.

10. Admittedly, the respondent Nos. 1-6 are not parties to the suit nor they have yet acquired any right, title, interest in the suit land on the basis of alleged agreement with the plaintiff dated 11-11-1995 pursuant to an ex parte decree dated 5-1-1985. Apart from the principle of lis pendens, the respondent Nos. 1-6 have not acquired any right, title, interest in the suit land. A person could only be impleaded as party to the suit under the provision of Order I, rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure which reads as under:

"All persons may be joined in one suit as plaintiffs in whom any right to relief in respect of or arising out of the same act or transaction or series of acts or transactions or alleged to exist, whether jointly, severally or in the alternative, where, if such persons brought separate suits, any common question of law or fact would arise."

11. From the above a person to be joined in a suit as the plaintiff is subject to two conditions, the right to relief must in each case be in respect of or arise out of the same act or transaction or series of acts or transactions alleged to exist, whether jointly, severally or in the alternative and where, if such persons brought separate suits, any common question of law or fact would arise.

12. Similarly, under the provision of Order I, rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure all persons may be joined as defendants against whom any right to relief in respect of or arising out of the same act or transaction or series of acts or in the alternative, where, if separate suits were brought against such persons, any common question of law or fact would arise.

13. Thus, the relief in respect of which parties may be joined must be relief arising out of the same set of circumstances or circumstances involving a common question of law or fact. It is, however, desirable to read Order II, rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure ie joinder of causes of action, as both Order I, rules 1 and 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure deal also to some extent with joinder of causes of action.

14. Under the provision of Order I, rule 10(b) of the Code of Civil Procedure the Court may strike out or add any parties as may appear to the Court to be just whether as the plaintiff or the defendant whose presence before the Court may be necessary in order to enable the Court effectually and completely to adjudicate upon and settle all the questions involved in the suit.

15. Respondent Nos. 1-6 though alleged to have entered into an agreement for sale dated 11-11-1995 pursuant to an ex parte decree in respect of the suit dated 5-1-1995 which has been set aside subsequently, could by no stretch of imagination claim any right to relief to enforce the case of action in respect of the suit, either as a plaintiff or as a defendant and, as such, they could neither be a proper nor necessary party to the suit whose presence before the Court may be necessary in order to enable the Court effectually and completely to adjudicate upon and settle the question involved in the suit.

16. The suit is a suit for specific performance of contract between the plaintiff and the defendant. Respondent Nos. 1-6 have alleged an agreement for sale between the plaintiff of the suit for specific performance of contract and themselves but the plaintiff has not yet acquired any right, title and interest in the suit land on the basis of his agreement for sale in respect of the suit land.

17. In the instant suit for specific performance of contract the respondent Nos. 1-6 have no right to relief for setting up an independent claim of title to the land beyond the cause of action of the suit which will disentitle them to be included in the suit within the frame of the present suit wherein the Rule in question is to be determined where the contract for sale was challenged/disputed and where, on the basis of the pleading of the parties thereof, the plaintiffs is entitled to get a decree.

18. In the case of Golam Kader vs Abdul Khaleque Choukder reported in 43 DLR (AD) 107 which arose out of a suit for Specific Performance of Contract in which the appellant filed an application under Order I, rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure stating that they are the plaintiffs in Title Suit No. 7 of 1969 that the plaintiffs of the present suit for Specific Performance of Contract created a collusive document in order to grab the property of Title Suit No. 7 of 1969 and further stating that they are necessary parties in the present suit and, as such, they should be added as defendants in the suit for ends of justice. It has been held in the aforesaid decision that:

"The present appellants are not claiming through the defendants of the present suit. They have set up an independent title of their own. Their averments in the application are for addition of party of the present suit. That will convert the present suit for specific performance of contract into a suit for determination of title which is not permissible in law. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division rightly found that the present appellants are not necessary parties for complete and effectual adjudication of the issues involved in the present suit."

19. Mr Md Fazlul Karim, the learned Counsel appearing for the respondents, however, referred to the decision in the case reported in AIR 1931 PC 162 for the proposition that under Order I, rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure the Courts adding a defendant as the plaintiff should always be adopted where it is necessary for a complete adjudication upon the question involved in the suit and to avoid multiplicity of the proceeding.

20. The said proposition is not disputed but as has been stated above, in the facts and circumstances of the case the said decision has no manner of application.

21. The respondent Nos. 1-6 would have no cause for concern to proceed with the instant suit in order to secure their interest on the basis of their alleged agreement with the plaintiff of the instant suit and in case the plaintiff did not proceed with the suit before the trial Court, the respondents may have a cause to be impleaded in the suit and to get themselves transposed as the plaintiff in the suit.

<u>22. Admittedly, the respondent Nos. 1-6 who are strangers to the instant suit could not proceed with the revisional application against the order passed allowing the amendment of the written statement having no locus standi/cause to contest the same. Furthermore, the plaintiff allegedly entered into an agreement for sale of the suit, land obtaining an ex parte decree for specific performance. Since the said decree has been set aside and the suit has been restored to its original file and number, until a decree is passed in favour of the plaintiff, no right would accrue to the respondent Nos. 1-6 over the suit land for enforcement of their alleged right under the agreement for sale with the plaintiff. They at the relevant time, being totally the strangers to the instant suit could neither be a party to the suit or entitled to be transposed as the petitioner in the revisional application to proceed with the Rule as they have no right to relief whatsoever therein.</u>

23. For the reasons stated above, the impugned order is not sustainable in law and the same is accordingly, set aside.

In the result the appeals are allowed but without any order as to costs.

End.

full_judgment:
This Rule at the instance of the added defendant arises out of an order dated 15-9-93 passed by the learned Additional Subordinate Judge, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 155 of 1992.

2. The facts relevant for the disposal of the Rule are that, one Pran Ballav Sarker instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 143 of 1969 in the Court of 1st Subordinate Judge, Dhaka, which, was transferred to the court of Additional Subordinate Judge, renumbered as Title Suit No. 155 of 1992 for declaration of title that the plaintiff is the sixteen annas owner of the suit land and further declaration that the decree obtained by the defendant Md Tayeb on 13-9-69 in Title Suit No. 166 of 1966 is a nullity on the averments that Fran Ballav purchased the land comprising plot No. 1749 and plot No. 3624 from Aswini Sarker and Ram Krishna Das and he became the owner of the suit land by purchase and by inheritance and the defendant Md. Tayeb obtained a fraudulent and collusive decree in Title Suit No. 166 of 1966 of the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka. The defendant has no right, title, interest and possession in the suit property.

3. The petitioner's case is that when the suit came to be ready for hearing it was brought to the notice of the court that Pran Ballav had died and in his place his daughter Malati Sarker was substituted. Subsequently the order of substitution was set aside as it revealed that Pran Ballav is still alive, who is residing in India was confirmed by the District Judge, 24 Parganas, West Bengal, It is further case of the petitioner that the opposite party No. 2 filed Title Suit No. 83 of 1971 claiming the suit property but the proceeding of the suit was stayed on the prayer of the defendant Md. Tayeb under section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The opposite party No.  2 made an application for being added as party which was opposed by the petitioner on the ground that the opposite party purchased the property after an order of injunction was passed. by the court restraining Pran Ballav from selling the property.

4. It appears that when the instant suit was proceeding the opposite party No. 2 Imamuddin filed an application under Order 1 rule 10(2), Order 22 rule 10(1) read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 2-5-92 praying for making him as plaintiff in the suit stating that Ballav Sarker (now deceased) instituted Title Suit No. 143 of 1969 on 19-5-69 in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka against Md. Tayeb being the defendant, who filed written statements and after his death his legal heir was substituted. Some other persons being purchasers from the said Md. Tayeb were also added as defendants in the suit. Subsequent to the filing of the suit the opposite party No. 2 Md Imamuddin purchased the suit property from the said Pran Ballav by registered Kabala being No. 4183 dated 20-5-1971 and entered into possession of the purchased land and he has been in possession of the said land. Opposite party No. 2 stated that the said Pran Ballav is said to have died and his daughter Sree Malati, Sarker being only legal heir was prosecuting the suit but recently it seemed to him that Malati being guided by ill motive is not taking any step in the suit nor she is attending the court and she is avoiding to take steps in the suit in order to defeat the interest of the petitioner (Opposite Party No. 2) in collusion with the defendants. It was further asserted that he purchased the suit property from Pran Ballav and acquired substantial interest in the suit property and that he being the plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 83 of 1971 in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka impleading the plaintiff and the principal defendant of the instant suit as defendant but on the prayer of the defendant under section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure the proceeding of the said suit was stayed, and, as such, he is required to be impleaded as plaintiff in the suit otherwise he will be very much prejudiced in his interest as there will be nobody to contest the suit and to represent his interest before the court.

5. Against the said petition one Golam Ali Imam Bhuiyan another defendant filed written objection contending that the application is barred under section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act. It was further stated that when the original plaintiff was not attending the court, the plaintiff's appointed lawyer filed an application falsely stating that Pran Ballav died on 9-11-75 leaving only daughter Malati Sarker and accordingly, Malati Sarker was substituted as plaintiff on 22-2-77. Subsequently, it transpired that Pran Ballav is alive and he is staying in West Bengal, India. On production of some papers including an affidavit sworn by Pran Ballav which was sent from India, the order of substitution was set aside, and the defendant was directed to bring Pran Ballav Sarker before the court within three months in default, to examine him on commission. Thereafter on the prayer of the defendant Tayeb the learned Court ordered for issuing letter of request on 8-11-79 for examining the plaintiff on commission. Against the said order Malati Sarker preferred a revision application but the order issuing letter of request was upheld up to the High Court Division. The letter of request was issued 24-3-87 to the learned District Judge 24 Parganas to examine the said Pran Ballav and the learned District Judge, 24 Parganas sent a report wherein it was mentioned that the family members of Pran Ballav told that Pran Ballah left the house for preaching religion. It was thus contended that Pran Ballav is still alive and as the original plaintiff is not willing to prosecute the suit, the said Imamuddin has no legal right to be impleaded as party in the suit and, as such, the application is liable to be rejected.

6. The learned Subordinate Judge, after hearing the parties passed the order dated 15-9-93 and thereby allowed the application under Order 22 rule 10(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure with a finding that the petitioner Imamuddin has the requisite qualification to be impleaded as party to the suit in the category of plaintiff as he has filed the kabala to prove his locus standi.

7. Although the opposite party No. 2 made the application referring Order I rule 10 (2), Order 22 rule 10(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure read with section 151 but the learned Subordinate Judge while making the order allowing the application wrongly quoted the order and it was written as Order 22 rule 10(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned Subordinate Judge, as it appears from the order itself, has not stated in so many words about the entitlement and the legal necessity of Imamuddin being impleaded as plaintiff in the suit but it has been categorically observed that the petitioner Imamuddin has the requisite qualification and locus standi to be impleaded as party to the suit in the category of plaintiff which leads to the conclusion that the opposite party No. 2 fulfills the legal requirements.

8. In this matter Mr. Younus Halder already argued the case on behalf of the petitioner. Mr. Fazlul Karim, the learned Counsel, appears today and submits that this is not the proper stage of the proceeding to implead the opposite patty No. 2 as plaintiff. He has argued that a letter of request was issued by the learned Court by order dated 8-11-79 for examining the said Pran Ballav and by that it will be ascertained whether the original plaintiff Pran Ballav is alive or dead and that order on challenge by Malati Sarker was upheld upto the High Court Division. But no report against letter of request has yet been sent to the trial Court, and in view of that unless that portion of the proceeding is exhausted the opposite party No. 2 has no legal footing to be impleaded as plaintiff in the suit. His further contention is that if any report is sent against that letter of request by the District Judge, 24 Parganas showing that Pran Ballav is dead, in that case Malati Sarker, the daughter of the original plaintiff will again be substituted and brought on record as plaintiff in due course to proceed with the suit. Mr. Fazlul Karim submits that there is still possibility of Malati Sarker being substituted in the suit, and as such, without exhausting rule 3 of Order 22 of the Code the court should not have resorted to apply Order 22 rule 10(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure in making the opposite party No. 2 as plaintiff in the suit. In support of this contention the learned Counsel has made reliance on the decisions in the case of Kedarnath Kanoria and ors vs. Khatian Sons & Co. reported in AIR 1959 (Cal) 368 and Gautarn De Sitamany vs. Madhavan Sivarajan, reported in AIR 1977 Kerala 83.

9. It appears from the pleading of the contending parties that Pran Ballav was said to have died and consequently his daughter Malati Sarker was substituted and brought on record and that ultimately it was found from the report sent by the District Judge, 24 Parganas that Pran Ballav is still alive and as a result the order for substitution was set aside. It is now admitted by the petitioner that Pran Ballav is alive and he is living in India. The allegation of the opposite party No. 2 is that Malati  Sarker being the daughter of original plaintiff is not taking any step in the suit and she is avoiding the proceeding of the suit in order to defeat the interest of the opposite party No. 2. It further appears that admittedly the opposite party No. 2 purchased the major portion of the suit property from the said Pran Ballav in the year 1971 i.e. subsequent to the filing of the suit. The purchase document was filed before the trial Court. It shows that he is an assignee and a right has accrued to him to seek leave of the Court to continue the suit or to be impleaded as party. Further, his grievance is that in the absence of original plaintiff Pran Ballav there will be nobody to prosecute the suit and consequently his substantial interest in the suit property will remain unrepresented in the proceeding and in that case his interest will be prejudiced. Ordinarily, it is not incumbent upon the assignee like the opposite party No. 2 to make an application during the pendency of the suit to be impleaded as plaintiff if the suit is continued by the original plaintiff. But in the instant case the undisputed fact is, that neither the original plaintiff nor his daughter is taking any interest to prosecute the suit resulting that his interest will not be looked after by his assignor his representative.

10. The suit is not one for mere declaration that the decree in Title Suit No. 166 of 1966 is a nullity. It is also for a declaration that the plaintiff is the 16 annas owner of the property to the suit. Had it been a suit for mere declaration that decree obtained in Title Suit No. 166 of 1966 is a nullity, in that case none excepting the persons who were parties to the decree and who were parties in the suit out of which the decree arose and their legal representatives were necessary parties. It is evident from the record that the present petitioner was also added as defendant being the purchaser from the original defendant Md. Tayeb. The contention that Imamuddin has no right to be impleaded as plaintiff as his interest is hit by the principle of res judicata is wholly untenable in that he is not being added as party in view of the provision of Order I rule 10(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure. Having regard to the fact that the original plaintiff is alive and the opposite party No. 2 is the assignee of the original plaintiff, I do not find any substance in the submission of Mr. Fazlul Karim. The cases cited cannot apply for the obvious reason that the applications in these cases were made after the suit had abated.

<u>11. The admitted position is that the opposite party No. 2 is an assignee being a subsequent purchaser during the pendency of the suit and he has acquired substantial interest in the suit property and, as such, he may be impleaded as plaintiff in ordinary course by the discretionary power of the court. Another aspect of the case is, that the suit instituted by the opposite party No. 2 was stayed on the application filed by the defendant and as the proceeding of his own suit has been stayed and there is nobody to represent his interest in the instant suit he may be impleaded as plaintiff in the suit.</u>

<u>12. The provision as laid down under Order 22 rule 10(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure does not contemplate the addition of a new party, but the person having interest obtained through purchase from a person who was a party in the suit, may be impleaded on enabling him to continue the suit. In the instant case the aforesaid provision was invoked when it was found that the original plaintiff is absent and there is no other person on his behalf to prosecute the suit. In the circumstances stated above the opposite party No. 2 being an assignee resorted to an alternative procedure which guarded against the danger that the original plaintiff being no longer interested in the suit may not prosecute the suit or may collide with defendants. The learned Subordinate Judge by exercising his judicial discretion made the order and thereby impleaded the opposite party No. 2 as plaintiff in the suit having regard to the fact that he has substantial interest in the property to the suit, This kind of judicial discretion is not always open to the revisional jurisdiction of the High Court Division unless the discretionary power is exercised arbitrarily or fancifully and unless the order is contrary to legal principles governing the exercise of such discretion.</u>

<u>13. The learned Subordinate Judge, considering the facts and circumstances of the case came to a conclusion that the opposite party No. 2 Imamuddin has locus standi and requisite qualification to be impleaded as plaintiff in the suit. In that view of the matter, the learned Subordinate Judge has not committed any error causing failure of justice in allowing the application under Order 22 rule 10(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, and I do not find any ground to interfere with the order passed by the learned Subordinate Judge.</u>

14. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs.

15. Stay granted by this court stands vacated.

Send down the records at once.

End.

full_judgment:
This Rule was issued on an application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure challenging the judgment and decree dated 25-6-1996 and 6-7-1996 respectively passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Noakhali, in Title Appeal No. 179 of 1992 affirming the judgment and decree dated 21-6-1992 and 27-6-1992 respectively passed by the Subordinate Judge Noakhali, in Title Suit No. 45 of 1984 dismissing the suit.

2. This revisional application arises out of the following facts: One Ana Miah Patwari and another Basu Mia Patwary instituted Title Suit No. 45 of 1984 challenging the decree of title Suit No. 60 of 1966 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Noakhali declaration of the decree passed on 16-5-1993 as collusive.

3. The opposite Party No. 1 as defendant contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the all material allegations in the plaint.

4. The Trial Judge dismissed the suit against which an appeal No. 179 of 1992 was preferred before the District Judge, Noakhali which was heard by the Additional District Judge who dismissed the appeal.

5. Being aggrieved by an dissatisfied with the aforesaid Judgment and decree of the appellate Court, the petitioner preferred this revisional application before this Court and obtained the present Rule.

6. Mr Md Nowab Ali, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submitted that the Courts below committed errors both in law and facts as both the Courts below came to wrong findings on perusal of the record of title suit No. 60 of 1966 the defendant No. 2 of the Title Suit No. 45 of 1984 filed written statement and vokalatanama though the PWs categorically denied to have any summons of the above TS No. 60 of 1966. The learned Subordinate Judge came to such finding on misconception of law as well as facts occasioning a failure of justice. The learned Subordinate Judge ought to have come to the finding that the plaintiffs did not know about their previous suits. He further submitted that all the PWs categorically denied to have any knowledge of Title Suit No. 44 of 1942 and Title Suit No. 60 of 1966 as no summons were served upon them appeared in any of the above suits by filing vokalatnama nor they have engaged any lawyer even none of them filed any written statement in Title Suit No. 60 of 1966 and none of them filed any Rafanama in Title Suit No. 44 of 1942. The signature of one Ana Miah Patwary was shown in the vokalatnama and on so-called vokalatnama by forgery with false personification as Ana Miah Patwary was an illiterate man and he did not know how to sign. But the learned subordinate Judge hopelessly failed to understand it. It was the duty of learned Trial Court to disbelieve the story of the defendants that Ana Miah Patwari put his signatures on the Rafanama in TS No. 44 of 1942. But the learned Subordinate Judge committed great error of law in holding that on perusal of record of both the Title Suit No. 44 of 1942 and TS No. 60 of 1966 it appeared to him that Ana Miah Patwary appeared in Court, took steps filed Rafanama in TS No. 44 of 1942 and also filed 'written statements in TS 60 of 1966 and the plaintiffs are in know about the above suits which occasioned a failure of justice in dismissing TS No. 45 of 1984. The learned Counsel also contends that the subsequent records of right and Dakhilas prove that the property in suit are in absolute possession of the plaintiffs having right, title and interest in the property. The learned Courts below have totally filed to consider these aspects of the suit. If there is existence of decree in TS No. 44 of 1942 then why they are not in possession and subsequent record-of-right was not prepared in their names. The non-consideration of this fact also occasioned failure of justice which vitiated the whole trial. In support of his contention he referred the decisions in the cases of Abul Khair Mia vs Abdul Latif Sardar, reported in 32 DLR (AD) 167, Abbas Ali Pramanik vs Gafur Ali Pramanik, reported in 27 DLR 249, Md Idris Khan vs Haji Erfanuddin, reported in 9 DLR 601 and Abdur Razzak Hawladar vs Sk Md Shafi, reported in 1994 BLD (SC) 119.

7. None appears for the opposite party.

<u>8. I have perused the materials on record and considered the submissions of the learned Counsel of the petitioner. 5 PWs and 3 DWs have been examined. On careful reading of the statements of the witnesses and judgments of the Courts below, it appeared to me that both the Courts below committed error in considering the facts, law related to this case and sifting properly the statement of the witnesses of both sides though the witnesses deposed supporting their respective cases. The trial Judge did not at all consider the position of the plaintiff No. 1 who was a proforma defendant No. 9 in title Suit No. 44 of 1942 and defendant No. 1 in title Suit No. 60 of 1966 was an illiterate man and even he did not know how to sign, then how he could put signature on the vokalatnama, written statement and Rafanama. The defendant did not cross-examine the PW 1 and other PWs on the point to find out that the plaintiff No. 1 Ana Miah Patwary was a literate man how he could sign. But the Subordinate Judge did not take any pain to ascertain the matter but he ought to have come to the findings that the plaintiff did not have the knowledge of TS No. 44 of 1942 and TS No. 60 of 1966 but the Subordinate Judge, acted most illegally for which the judgment and decree should be set aside and the plaintiffs suit be decreed. The same error was also committed by the appellate Court. The argument advanced by the learned Counsel has also legal value that the defendant claimed the suit land through a pattanama which was executed and registered by landlord's predecessors of the plaintiff Noor Jahan Begum and Asamuddin Patwary granting some lands to Ashraf Ali Bepari and Yosuf Ali Bepari. In the putta the Zamindars (who were also illiterate) reserved the right of transfer by the pattandars in favour of the Zamindars or their heirs and none else. The transfer by the Pattandars or by their heirs are prohibited. In the pattan name the transfer made by the pattandar or their heirs are illegal and void and by the transfer of the pattandars or their heirs the transferees got no title in the property. This aspect of law has not been taken into consideration by the Courts below which is vital point of law. On the basis of above facts I find perverse in the judgment of the Courts below, non-reading of the statements of the witnesses and wrong explanation of Municipal Law related to the case. So, the judgments of the Courts below should be interfered by invoking revisional jurisdiction. The references given by the learned Counsel are also applicable in the case and his submission of learned Counsel has also substance and force. The Rule has merit.</u>

9. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The Judgments and decrees of both the Courts below are hereby set aside.

Send down the lower Court records at once.

End.
