full_judgment:
Siddiqur Rahman Miah J: This provisional application at the instance of the plaintiffs appellants is directed against the judgment and decree dated 23-3-2004 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, First Court, Camilla, in Title Appeal No. 206 of 2001 dismissing the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 31-10-2001 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Camilla, who dismissed the Title Suit No. 8 of 2001.

2. The petitioners as plaintiffs instituted the title suit for declaration of title and recovery of Khas possession imp leading the opposite parties as defendants.

3. The case of the plaintiffs, in brief, is that, one Fazle Ali Mridha was the owner of the land stated in the 1st and 2nd schedules to the plaint and the CS khatian No. 673 was accordingly, prepared in his name; that thereafter he mortgaged first schedule land to Wahidullah, the predecessor of the plaintiffs in consideration of Taka 200 and that required "Tamshuk Patra Dalil" was registered on 13-6-1929 copulating interest to be paid Taka 1.50% per month and also stipulated that Fazle Ali Mridha would not transfer to other person unless the consideration money would be paid along with interest. It is further contended that Fazle Ali could not realise the aforesaid money and moreover, he created a "Belawaznama" deed in favour of his two wives namely, Atarernessa Bibi and Nekjan Bibi and also created a 'Safkabala' deed in favour of his foster daughter Hasmaternessa Bibi and son-in-law Nadir Ali in respect of the suit land for the purpose of saving the suit land from further auction sale due to his deftness; that in this circumstances Wahidullah filed a Arbitration Case No. 83 of 1938 against Fazle Ali Mridha to realize the cot money; that Fazle Ali Mridha admitted about the debt but later on he died before realization of debt; that the heirs of Fazle Ali Mridha i.e. his two wives, foster daughter and son-in-law sold the property to Wahidullah vide registered kabala deed dated 4-4-1940 in consideration of Taka 300 amongst which Taka 200 was setoff with the debt and received rest of Taka 100 and handed over the possession of the land to Wahidullah and that the aforesaid heirs of Fazle Ali Mridha sold the 2nd schedule land to Wahidullah vide registered deed dated 18-6-1941. It is also added that having the ownership of the land, Wahidullah died leaving behind plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 and plaintiff Nos. 8 to 10 and others and accordingly, SA record was prepared in the names of his sons and daughters; that thereafter the Tasdik record was also prepared in the names of plaintiffs; that in the meantime the plaintiff No. 1 constructed semi-pucca building in the plot No. 2065 in the year of 1991 and 1992 and started to live there appointing one Babul Miah as caretaker and that a holding No. 38 /Ka was opened in Laksham Pourashava in the name of plaintiff No. 1 as the house was created in schedule No. 2ka and 2Kha . The further case of the plaintiffs is that defendant Nos. 1, 5, 6, 7 and 10 to 12 hired persons and threatened to dispossess the caretaker Babul Mia and that then Babul Mia lodged a GD entry with Laksham Police Station and that police held enquiry and filed an application before the Magistrate Court for appointing a receiver. The Magistrate appointed the Officer-in-Charge of Laksham Police Station as receiver. The receiver on 27-5-1997 attached the suit property in preparing seizure list. Thereafter, the defendants filed Criminal Revision case before the learned District Judge for setting aside the appointment of receiver with direction to hand over the possession to the defendants, then the aforesaid caretaker ran up to the Appellate Division but all went in vain.

4. The plaintiffs alleged that at the time of preparation of seizure list, the defendant No. 1 managed to write in the seizure list that he took possession from the defendants but the fact is that the plaintiffs have been in possession of the suit land on 28-1-2001 when the receiver took over the possession and thus the plaintiffs were constrained to file the suit for declaration of title and recovery of khans possession.

5. The opposite party No. 1 as the defendant No. 1 entered appearance and contested the suit in filing written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint stating, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable in this form and manner; that the same is barred by limitation; that Fazle Ali was the owner of the suit land and chitin was also prepared in his name; that Fazle Ali gifted some of the suit land to his two wives namely, Atarernessa Bibi and Nakjan Bibi vide registered Belewaz deed dated 26-9-1939 and also transferred rest property to his foster daughter Hasmaternessa i.e. the mother of the defendants, and to Nader Ali i.e. the father of the defendants, and that thereafter Atarernessa and Nekjan Bibi orally gifted their land to the parent of defendants and that in this circumstances Hasmaternessa and Nader Ali started to live in 2nd scheduled land i.e. on the bank of pond, situated in plot No. 2085. It is further stated that during their possession, Wahidullah, the father of the plaintiffs, disclosed about the alleged debt, then Hasmaternessa and Nader Ali were constrained to execute two security deeds dated 31-3-1940 and 18-6-1941 in the form of safkabala deed as they had no money at that time; that it was stipulated that if Hasmaternessa and others would repay the debt money, then Wahidullah would return the land to them and accordingly, Hasmaternessa repaid Taka 400 to Wahidullah in the year 1943 but could not get registration of reconveyance deed due to want of registration expenses and; that since then the heirs of Hasmaternessa and Nader Ali have been possessing the land; that subsequently, the defendant Nos. 1 to 4 constructed the tin-shed building after demolishing the old house of the defendants in plot No. 2085 and started to live there in paying the rent and taxes and that Wahidullah did not acquire any right and title in the suit land as the deeds dated 31-3-1940 and 18-6-1941 were nothing but security deeds and that in this circumstances the instant suit is liable to be dismissed.

6. At the trial, the plaintiffs examined 4 witnesses. PW 1 is Ekramullah who is plaintiff No. 1, PW 2 is Taieb Ali, aged about 65 years, who knew the father of the plaintiffs and who had knowledge about transaction. PW 3, Md Siddique, knows the parties who deposed about the previous possession of the plaintiffs, PW 4, Babul Mia, was the caretaker of the plaintiffs who filed the application under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure who fought up to the Appellate Division on behalf of the plaintiffs and all facts of possession and dispossession of the plaintiffs were in the know of him.

7. The plaintiffs filed CS khatian (Exhibit 1), deed dated 31-3-1940 executed by Atarernessa in favour of Md. Wahidullah (Exhibit 2), deed dated 18-6-1941 executed by Atarernessa in favour of Wahidullah (Exhibit 3), deed dated 9-6-1949 executed by Badsha Miah in favour of Wahidullah (Exhibit 4), SA khatian (Exhibit 5), Dakhilas (Exhibit 6, 6(ka) to 6(Na), tax receipts of Pourashava (Exhibit 7), certificate given by Chairman, Pourshava (Exhibit 7(Ka) and certified copy of the judgment and decree in title Suit No. 356 of 1994 of Subordinate Judge Court (Exhibits 8 and 8(Ka)) in support of their contention.

8. The defendants examined 3(three) witnesses DW 1, Shafiqur Rahman, is defendant No. 1 who narrated the case of the defendants. DW 2 is Serajul Islam who knows the parties and the suit land and he deposed about the possession of the defendants. DW 3, Abdul Mannan, who deposed supporting the possession of the plaintiffs.

9. The defendants have filed the certified copy of the judgment in criminal revision No. 111 of 1997 (Exhibit Ka), the certified copy of the Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 507 of 1998 and some receipts of Laksham Municipality (Exhibits Ga and Ga(1)) in support of their contention.

10. Upon pleadings, the learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Comilla framed the following issues for disposal of the case:

1. Is the suit maintainable in its present form?

2. Is the suit barred by limitation ?

3. Is the suit bad for defect of parties ?

4. Have the plaintiffs right and title in the suit land ?

5. Are the plaintiffs entitled to get relief’s as prayed for ?

11. The learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Comilla, upon hearing and on perusal of evidence, dismissed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 31-10-2001 stating that though the plaintiffs have proved their title in the suit land by virtue of two deeds of Wahidullah Chowdhury but they did not get possession on the basis of the said deeds and the plaintiffs also have failed to prove their possession before taking of the suit land by the receiver.

12. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree dated 31-10-2001, the plaintiffs as appellants preferred Title Appeal No. 206 of 2001 before the learned District Judge, Comilla. On transfer the appeal was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, First Court, Comilla, who dismissed the appeal affirming the judgment and decree of the Joint District Judge taking the same view as was taken by the learned trial Court to the effect that the plaintiffs have failed to prove their possession on the basis of two title deeds and that as the plaintiffs have failed to prove their possession in the suit land, so they cannot get decree of recovery of khas possession.

13. It is against the aforesaid impugned judgment and decree dated 23-3-2004, the petitioner moved this Court and obtained the present Rule.

14. Mr Mahbubey Alam, on behalf of Mr Sarder Abul Hossain, appearing for the petitioners, has placed before us the judgment and decree of both the trial and appellate Courts, deposition of PWs and DWs and the papers filed by both the parties and submits that both the Courts below found title of the plaintiffs in the suit land but the learned Courts below totally failed to assess the evidence; that normally the concurrent findings of the Courts below cannot be disturbed when there is no allegation of misreading and nonbearing of evidence but where there is serious allegation of misreading and no reading of evidence and the judgments of the Courts below are founded on misconception of law or misinterpretation of documents, Revisional Court can legally interfere on the concurrent findings of Courts below. Mr Alam further submits that the learned Courts below committed an error both in law as well as on facts; that the Courts seriously failed to assess the evidence of witnesses and their Judgments are based on misconception of law and misinterpretation of documents, thus their decisions caused serious miscarriage of justice.

15. The learned Advocate for the petitioners relies upon a case of Akhter Hosain Shariff and others vs Munshi Akkas Hossain and others reported in 1983 BLD (AD) 334.

16. Mr Golam Arshad, on behalf of Mr Md Rafiqul Islam for the opposite-party No. 1, on the other hand, submits that the learned Court below, assessing the evidence on record, rightly found that the plaintiffs had no possession in the suit land on the basis of two deeds dated 31-3-1940 and 18-6-1941 and they also correctly found that the plaintiffs were not in possession when the receiver took possession of the suit land. Mr Golam Arshad further submits that the learned appellate Court was perfectly justified in passing impugned judgment and decree dated 23-3-2004 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree of the trial Court and that since the impugned judgment and decree do not suffer from any illegality so the provisional Court should not interfere in the impugned judgment and decree.

17. Mr Golam Arshed, the learned Advocate for the opposite party No.1, relied upon a decisions in the case of Mukbul Ahmed vs Oliuddin Bhuiyan and others reported in 1 BLC (AD) 175; the case of Ganaprojatantri Bangladesh Sarker represented by the DC, Bakergonj vs Joinal Abedin Dewan and others reported in 1 BLC (AD) 26; the case of Rupe Jahan Begum and others vs Lutfe Ali Chowdhury reported in 2 BLC (AD) 32; the case of Payari Mohan Das and others vs Rajjabernessa and others reported in 2 BLC 471; the case of lqbal Hossain Talukder (Md) vs Md Joinal Abedin Talukder and 76 others reported in 55 DLR 604 and the case of Jashimuddin Kanchan (Md) vs Md Ali Ashraf reported in 42 DLR (AD) 289 in support of his contention.

18. The moot question that calls for our determination in this case is, whether the learned Additional District Judge committed any error of law in dismissing the appeal on affirming the judgment and decree of the trial Court.

19. It is admitted that the suit land appertaining to CS khatian No. 673 originally belonged to Fazle Ali Mridha who mortgaged the same to Wahiduddin, the predecessor of the plaintiffs and that a Tamshuk patra deed was registered on 13-6-1929 to that end. It is also admitted that Fazle Ali Mridha without repaying mortgage money transferred some portion of the suit land in favour of his two wives namely, Atorernesga and Nekjan Bibi and by a habanera deed also transferred the other portion in favour of his foster daughter and son-in-law and that in the circumstances, Wahidulah filed an Arbitration case against Fazle Ali Mridha to realise the cot money.

20. Thus, case of the plaintiffs is that Fazle Ali Mridha admitted about the debt but before realization of debt, he died; that in order to repay the debt, the heirs of Fazle Ali Mridha i.e. two wives, foster daughter and son-in-law sold the suit property to Wahidullah vide two registered cabalas dated 4-4-1940 and 18-6-1941 and delivered possession of the suit land to him and that Wahidullah died leaving the plaintiffs in whose names SA record and later on Tasdik record was prepared, that the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit constructing semi-pucca building in plot No. 2085 appointing Babul Mia as caretaker till taking over the possession by the Receiver and that a Municipal holding being No. 38/Ka was opened and on the basis of which the plaintiffs paid municipal taxes.

21. SA record, mutation rent receipts, tax receipts in respect of suit land of the plaintiffs though not the evidence of title, these are clearly the evidence of possession, yet title follows possession. Onus is upon the defendants to rebut such presumption, but the defendants have totally failed to rebut such presumption. We receive support of the above view in case reported in 35 DLR (AD) 216 and 38 DLR 327.

22. The plaintiffs have filed CS khatian Exhibit 1, deed dated 31-3-1940 executed by Atorernessa in favour of Md Wahidullah, Exhibit 2, deed dated 18-6-1941 executed by Atorernessa in favour of Wahidullah.

23. On the other hand, the contention of the defendants is that the deeds dated 4-4-1940 and 18-6-1941 executed by the heirs of Fazle Ali Mridha were not the out and out sale deeds and those deeds were mere security deeds which were executed as a token of security and that mortgage money was later on paid but no deed was taken from the plaintiffs.

24. The pertinent question in this case is, whether these deeds are save kabala deeds or security deeds and whether possession on the basis of these deeds were delivered.

25. The plaintiffs stoutly deny such assertion of the defendant that those deeds were security deed as nothing was mentioned like this in the deeds. As per the provision of section 101 of the Evidence Act, the burden of proof lies on the party who substantially asserts the affirmative of the issue and not upon the party who denies it. The party on whom the onus of proof lies must, in order to succeed, establish a prima facie case. He cannot, on failure to do so, take advantage of the weakness of his adversary's case. He must succeed by the strength of his own right and the clearness of his own proof.

<u>26. The recital of the kabala dated 31-3-1940 and 18-6-1941 executed by the heirs of Fazle Ali in favour of Wahidullah speaks that these are out and out sale deeds. No where in the deeds, there is mention of security deeds. The plaintiffs by adducing evidence has successfully proved that these are out and out sale deeds which were executed with a view to meet up the debt of their predecessors. The defendants have totally failed to prove that these were the security deeds and thus, the defendants have failed to discharge the burden reposed on them. Basing on the evidence on record, both the trial as well as appellate Court concurrently held that those deeds are not the deeds of security, rather out and out sale deeds. We also affirm the concurrent findings of Courts below.</u>

27. The main dispute which centers round this case is, that who was in possession of the suit. The plaintiffs claim that they have been possessing the suit land on the basis of those deeds till taking over the possession of suit land by the Receiver on 28-1-2001.

28. On the other hand, contention of the defendants is that no title was passed by virtue of those deeds and that the plaintiffs or their predecessors were never in the possession of the suit land.

29. The learned Courts below concurrently found the title of the plaintiffs in the suit land but the plaintiffs' predecessors did not get possession on the basis of deeds dated 31-3-1940 and 18-6-1941.

30. Mr Golam Arshed, citing some decisions, submits that the revisional Court has no jurisdiction to interfere with the concurrent findings of the Courts below. He referring the decisions mentioned above, submits that the consistent views of all the decisions are that concurrent findings of the trial Court and of the appellate Court are not generally interfered if the findings do not suffer from misreading and no reading of evidence and misconception of law and that there is no allegation on misreading and non-reading of evidence. It is found that all the above decisions are condition precedent. It is a fact that decisions of the Court of appeal being last Court of fact are not open to interference in Revisional jurisdiction unless it is shown that the same have been based upon gross misreading of evidence or founded on misconception or misapplication or misapprehension of law or of any misinterpretation of any material document or otherwise perverse being contrary to law, and material evidence and materials on record.

31. The main object of section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure is to see whether Courts below committed any error of law resulting in an error in their decision occasioning failure of justice. If the revisional Court is not empowered with the power of seeing legality and propriety which occurred due to misreading and non-reading of evidence both oral and documentary and misconception of law, then administration of justice will suffer a lot.

<u>32. In view of the above discussion, we are of the view that the revisional Court has ample jurisdiction to review the concurrent findings of Courts below in order to see whether those Courts have committed any error of law which resulted in any failure of justice.</u>

<u>33. In the instant case, it is the allegation of plaintiffs-petitioners that both the trial Court or the appellate Court failed to assess both oral and documentary evidence and to misconceive he law bearing with the case. Now let us see how far such assertions of the plaintiffs are true.</u>

<u>34. In the recitals of the deeds dated 31-3-1940 and 18-6-1941 marked exhibits 2 and 3, there is clear assertion that the vendors of the deeds executed the same for repaying the debt and they categorically asserted that they or their successors would not claim the suit land in future. After such assertion, the claim of the defendants that the vendor did not deliver possession to the vendee does not lie. The defendants have totally failed to show any evidence that the possession of the suit land were not delivered on the basis of those deeds.</u>

35. On the other hand, PW 1 Ekramullah Chowdhury, son of Wahidullah Chowdhury, deposed that his father purchased the suit by virtue of kabala dated 4-4-1940 and kabala dated 18-6-1941 and got possession of the suit land; that after getting possession, he sold one decimal from plot No. 2077 and 48 decimals from plot No. 2078 to Tarab Ali and others who have been possessing the land since purchase, that his father also sold 49.5 decimals to Badsha Miah by virtue of Kabala dated 1-6-1949 and thus Badsha Miah has been possessing some portion of the suit land peacefully. He further deposed that he had been possessing the rest of the suit land creating semi-pucca building and tin-shed house thereon till taking over the possessing by the Receiver on 28-1-2001; that SA khatian being No. 691 Exhibit 5 was prepared in their names; that they paid rent and rent receipts were marked Exhibit 6 series; that during Bangladesh survey their names were recorded; that his brother also sold 23½ decimals of land to Torab Ali who has been also possessing the same; that Municipal holding was prepared in their names and they paid taxes and their tax receipts are marked Exhibit 7 series. He further testified that when defendants No. 1, 5 to 7 and others attempted to dispossess the caretaker of the plaintiffs on 17-5-1997, then the caretaker filed a GD entry in Laksham PS on 21-5-1997; that on the basis of the report of OC Laksham, Magistrate appointed OC, Laksham as Receiver who took possession from his care-taker; but being biased Officer-in-Charge, Laksham reported that he took possession of the defendants' land; that subsequently, appointment of Receiver was cancelled who handed over possession of the suit land to the defendant Nos. 1 to 4 and that the defendants had no possession before taking possession from the Receiver. Nothing could be elicited to shake his credibility in any manner whatsoever.

36. PW 2, Torab Ali, corroborating PW 1, deposed that he knew plaintiffs' father who purchased the suit land from two wives, foster daughter and son-in-law of Fazle Ali; that he having title and possession in the suit land sold 88 decimals of land to Badsha Miah who again sold the same to Abdul Majid and others who are in possession of the suit land; that brother of plaintiffs namely, Salimullah Chowdhury sold 26 decimals of land to him from plot Nos. 2077 and 2078 and that he also purchased some land from the wife of Badsha Miah and that he has been possessing the purchased land, erecting huts thereon. He further testified that the plaintiffs were in possession of the suit land before taking possession by the Receiver and the defendants had no possession before giving possession by the Receiver.

37. PW 3 Md Siddique deposed that he knows the plaintiffs, the defendants and the suit land; that the plaintiffs have tin-shed and cook shed in the suit land which was erected in year 1991; that Babul Miah was caretaker and that the plaintiffs were in possession of the suit land before taking possessing by the Receiver.

38. PW 4, Babul Miah, the caretaker, testified that he knows the plaintiffs, defendants and the suit land; that he was appointed as caretaker; that the plaintiffs have a tinted and cook shed house in the suit land and suit land was their paternal property; that Receiver took possession from him; that Receiver delivered possession to the defendants about 7 months ago and before that period, they had no possession in the suit land.

39. In the cross-examination, he again stoutly deposed that Receiver took possession from him on 28-1-2001.

<u>40. From the evidence of PWs, it reveals that the father of the plaintiffs namely, Wahidullah Chowdhury, purchased the suit land by two saf kabalas from two wives, foster daughter and son-in-law of Fazle Ali Mridha and took possession thereon. SA record was correctly prepared in the names of the plaintiffs on the basis of those kabalas. The plaintiffs and his father sold some portion of the suit land to different persons who also are in possession of their purchased land. The plaintiff had been possessing the suit land till when possession was taken by the Receiver. The plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land creating huts thereon, mutating their names, opening municipal holding, paying rent and municipal taxes.</u>

<u>41. SA record, mutation, rent receipts and tax receipts in respect of suit land of the plaintiffs though not evidence of title, these are clearly the evidence of possession, yet title follows possession. Onus is upon the defendants to rebut such presumption, but the defendants has totally failed to rebut such presumption. We receive support of the above view in cases reported 35 DLR (AD) 216 and 38 DLR 327.</u>

<u>42. The plaintiffs have proved their possession till taking over the possession by the Receiver and such assertion has not only been proved by oral evidence but also by documentary evidence. SA khatian and draft khatian of Bangladesh were prepared in the names of the plaintiffs. Mutation, opening of municipal holding, rent receipts and municipal taxes are also the documentary evidence of possession.</u>

43. It is surprising that both the Courts below totally failed to look into these oral and documentary evidence. The learned Courts below also have illegally relied upon the evidence of criminal proceedings without going through the evidence of this case.

44. In this connection Mr Alam refers the decision in the case Akhter Hosain Shariff and others vs Munshi Akkas Hossain and others reported in 1983 BLD (AD) 334. Referring the above decision he submits that both the Courts below committed illegality basing on the evidence of criminal proceedings without assessing the evidence of this case as regard the evidence of possession. Here in this case the Court is to see whether the plaintiffs were in possession of the suit land immediately before taking possession by the Receiver. It is the allegation of the plaintiffs that the Receiver took possession from his caretaker, Babul Miah, but the receiver being biased stated in his report that he took possession of the suit land from the defendants. The plaintiffs in this case has successfully proved that possession of the suit land was taken from the caretaker of the plaintiffs. But the learned Courts below failed to assess the evidence on this point, rather they have based on the findings of criminal Courts. The findings of the criminal Courts are not the findings on the civil Courts. The object of proceedings under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is to prevent breach of peace. Civil Court is entitled to pass findings as regard the title and possession and the decision of the competent civil Court are final in respect of the title and possession of the land in dispute. An order under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure cannot therefore, be treated as substantive evidence of title and possession. The findings of the Courts below are totally contrary to the evidence and law.

<u>45. In the facts and circumstances and evidence on record, we have no hesitation to find that both the Courts below failed to apply their respective judicial mind in passing their respective judgments. They passed the judgment without assigning any good reasons. We find illegality in the impugned judgment occasioning failure of justice to justify interference by this Court exercising revisional jurisdiction under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure. We find substance in the revision.</u>

46. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 23-3-2004 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, First Court, Comilla dismissing the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 31-10-2001 passed by the Joint District Judge, First Court, Comilla are set aside. The suit is decreed and the Plaintiffs do get khas possession of the suit land.

The defendant-opposite parties are directed to hand over the suit land within 30 days failing which plaintiffs-petitioner will get the possession of suit land as per the provision of law.

Send down the LCR at once.

End.

lawyer:
Sheikh Razzak Ali, Senior Advocate, instructed by Md. Sajjadul Huq, Advocate-on-Record — For the Petitioner.

VS

case_source: (From the Judgment and Order dated 19th August 1996 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3319 of 1995)
full_judgment:
Md Abdur Rouf J: Plaintiff Benode Bihari Mondal along with respondent No. 7-9 namely, Deben Mondal, Hazari Mondal and Sreemoti Tota Dasi Tarafder respectively as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 374 of 1987, in the Court of Munsif, 1st Court , Khulna against the defendant-respondents for setting aside the rent decree passed on 11-6-41 in Rent Suit No. 676 of 1941 of the Court of Munsif, 1st Court , Khulna and the auction sale held thereunder on 16-9-41 in Rent Execution Case No. 827 of 1941 of the suit property, on the ground that the impugned decree had been passed against a dead person namely, Fakir Chand Mondal. On being transferred the suit was re-numbered as Title Suit No. 5 of 1988 of the Court of Assistant Judge, Batiaghata.

2. Plaintiff's case, in short, is that, the suit jote comprising of 14.53 acres of land, appertains to CS Khatian 82 within Mouza Mailmara, Batiaghata, Khulna, originally belonged to Obhiram Sarder and Rupchand Sarder in equal share. Plaintiffs-predecessor Arjun Mondal, Fakir Mondal, Sonatan Mondal, Chandra Kanta Mondal and Jogheswar Mondal were bargadars under Obhiram and others and accordingly, their names were recorded as dakhalders in respect of 11.76 acres of land in the relevant record. Rupchand died leaving behind two sons namely. Ram Charan Sarder and Ram Krishna Sarder. Obhiram died leaving behind two sons namely, Gurucharan and Ramkanta Sarder. There was a dispute in between Gurucharan and others with that of plaintiffs' predecessor and to settle the dispute a bandabasta was made in respect of the suit property by a registered kabala dated 17-5-39 with the stipulation that the predecessor of the plaintiffs would deliver them either 60 shali paddy or a sum of Rs 300.00 annually. Plaintiffs as the successive heirs of aforesaid Arjun Mondal and others have possessed the suit land. The defendants on 1-11-86 threatened to dispossess the plaintiffs from the suit land. Hence the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 78 of 1986 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge 2nd Court, Khulna for declaration of their title to the suit land. In that suit defendants 14 to 16 in their written statement, filed on 27-6-87, disclosed that in pursuance of the aforesaid ex parte rent decree, the suit property was auction sold in execution of the said decree and on the basis of the auction purchase they claimed title to the suit land. Plaintiffs having come to know the aforesaid rent suit and the auction sale for the first time from the aforesaid written statement of the defendants, filed the present suit alleging, inter alia, that one of their predecessors namely, Fakir Mondal, a judgment debtor of the rent suit, had died on 28-12-39 before institution of the said rent suit, hence the rent decree and the alleged auction sale, held thereunder are nullity and that the alleged auction purchaser was never in possession of the suit land.

3. Defendant Nos. 11 and 12 also contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the case of the plaintiffs stating, inter alia, that Rup Chand, son of Obhiram Sarder, the original owner, and his other co-sharers had settled the suit land on 17-5-39 in favour of plaintiffs-predecessor Arjun Mondal and others and that the landlords also got a rent decree for arrears of rent in Rent Suit No. 676 of 1941 from the Court of Munsif, First Court, Khulna and in execution of the decree in Rent Execution Case No. 827 of 1941 the suit land was sold in auction on 16-9-41 which was confirmed on 11-11-41 and the auction purchaser got the writ of delivery of possession on 26-11-41. Thereafter plaintiffs-predecessor. Chandrakanta filed Misc. Case No. 275 of 1941 for setting aside the aforesaid auction sale which was dismissed on 7-3-42 and Misc. Appeal No. 69 of 1942 filed by said Chandra Kanta was also dismissed by the learned District Judge, Khulna on 26-5-42. Thereafter Jogeswar Mondal, another predecessor of the plaintiffs, also filed Misc. Case No. 171 of 1942 in the Court of Munsif, 3rd Court, Khulna under section 173(3) of the Bengal Tenancy Act which was also dismissed on 10-2-43. They also denied the plaintiffs are the heirs of Arjun Mondal. According to them, Fakir Mondal died after the auction sale and they claimed the suit land by inheritance.

4. Defendant Nos. 14 to 16 also contested the suit by filing another written statement and claimed that on 8-4-70 they had purchased 3.63 acres of land out of the suit land from Ramkrishna and they have been possessing the same. Their further case is Ramchandra died leaving behind his only son Kanak Sarder who having left this country for India for ever his share in the suit property has been vested in the Government as non-resident property and the same is being leased out by the Government to different persons in Misc. Case No. 28 of 1976-77.

5. The trial Court decreed the suit on 19-4-93 holding, inter alia, that the plaintiffs came to know of the alleged auction sale on 27-6-87 from the written statement of Defendant Nos. 14-16 filed in Title Suit No. 78 of 1986 and that the suit is not barred by limitation and that the summons of the rent suit and the execution case were not served upon the plaintiffs-predecessor. In allowing Title Appeal No. 130 of 1993, on 16-3-94, preferred by defendant Nos. 1-6, the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Khulna sent back the case on remand to the trial Court. Whereupon the present petitioner moved the High Court Division in revision against the said order of remand and obtained a Rule, Civil Revision No. 2197 of 1994. A Single Bench of the High Court Division after setting aside that judgment directed the lower appellate Court to dispose of the appeal on merit. Thereafter the lower appellate Court by its judgment and decree dated 26-6-95 reversed the judgment and decree of the trial Court and dismissed the suit. The plaintiffs-petitioner then again moved the High Court Division in revision against the judgment and decree of the lower appellate Court and obtained a Rule, Civil Revision 3319 of 1995, and by the impugned judgment and order dated 1996 a Single Bench of the High Court Division has discharged the Rule and upheld the judgment and decree of the lower appellate Court.

6. The plaintiff-petitioner now seeks leave to appeal from the said judgment of the High Court Division.

7. Sheikh Razzak Ali, learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that Fakir Mondal, father of plaintiff No. 2 Hazari Mondal, one of the judgment-debtors in the rent decree, although had died on 28-12-39 long before institution of the rent suit but a fraudulent decree was obtained in the Rent Suit showing him alive and accordingly the auction sale of the property in execution of the decree was illegally held. Mr. Ali further submitted that the plaintiff by producing the extract of the death register Exhibit 6, proved that Fakir Mondal died on 28-12-39 and that the trial Court on consideration of both oral and documentary evidence accepted the said Ext. 6 as genuine but the lower appellate Court upon misreading Exhibit 6 and the evidence of PW 4 wrongly held that Exhibit 6 is not a genuine document. In support of his submission Mr. All sought to show that in Ext. 6 father's name of Fakir Mondal has been mentioned and in column 1 thereof it is mentioned that Fakir Mondal died of "Ulautha".

<u>8. It appears from the judgment of the lower appellate Court that the learned Judge upon assigning several reasons rightly doubted the genuineness of Exhibit 6 and reversed the finding of the trial Court that Fakir Mondal had died before passing of the rent decree and the auction sale and further held that Fakir Mondal died after the passing of the rent decree and the alleged auction sale. The learned Judge of the High Court Division in the facts and circumstance of the instant case in exercise of his revisional jurisdiction does not appear to have committed any illegality in upholding the said finding of the lower appellate Court, which is based upon the evidence on record, in maintaining the judgment and decree of the lower appellate Court. The submission of Mr. All having boiled around the appreciation of evidence, which appears to have correctly been done by the lower appellate Court, we do not find any substance in this petition.</u>

It is, therefore, dismissed.

End.

lawyer:
Shamsuddin Babul with Kanai Lal Shaha, Advocates -For the Petitioners

parties:
Abdul Hannan and another ------ Petitioners

full_judgment:
An order dated 19-10-1995 recorded by learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 4 Dhaka in Title Suit No. 298 of 1992 allowing amendment of plaint on reviewing order dated 27-3-1994 recorded on the strength of an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure is under challenge in this Civil Revisional Petition under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

2. The fact of Civil Revisional petition hinges on answer to the following question, whether the order under challenge in Revision dated 19-10-1995 reviewing the order dated 27-3-1994 on the basis of an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure is well founded on law and the same warrants any interference by this Court in the exercise of Civil Revisional Authority under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

3. A resume of facts essential and requisite to dispose of the question is stated hereunder.

4. Opposite Party Nos.1 to 5 of this Civil Revisional petition as plaintiffs laid a suit being Title Suit No.126 of 1974 in the Fifth Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for declaration of title on the property described in schedule to the plaint and also for a decree of khas possession on removing construction constructed thereon. The said suit was renumbered as Title Suit No. 298 of 1992 on transfer to the Court of Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka. Averments made in the plaint are that Md Yasin Bepari had been owner and possessor of the property recorded in Cadestral Survey Khatian Nos.10 and 11. Md Yasin Bepari died leaving behind two sons, Abdul Hamid and Amirullah and three daughters Jiashbi Bibi, Hashrabi Bibi and Nanna Bibi and wife Anrabi Bibi, and sons, daughters and wife became owners and possessors of the said property. Abdul Hamid, the heir son of Md Yasin Bepari, became owner and possessor of the property of Cadestral Survey plot No.8587 of Cadestral Survey Khatian Nos.10 and 11 measuring 2.46 acres by way of several deeds of transfer from other heirs of Md Yasin Bepari. Abdul Hamid Bepari, thereafter, transferred the said 2.46 acres of property in favour of predecessor mother of the plaintiffs, Syeda Salima Noorjahan Begum by a deed of conveyance dated 13-9-1932. On the death of Syeda Salima Noorjahan Begum, plaintiffs as legal heirs inherited the said property and remained owners and possessors of the said property. Defendants got no title and possession over that 2.46 acres of property. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 on the strength of sale deed dated 1-1-1971 from Jumratan Bibi, alleged daughter of Md Yasin Bepari, entered unauthorisedly on the property described in schedule-Kha to the plaint. The schedule Kha property will be referred to hereinafter as suit property. Md Yasin Bepari got no daughter named Jumratan Bibi. The deed of defendants are forged, fraudulent and on the basis of that deed defendants did not acquire any title on the suit property.

5. Petitioner of Civil Revision petition as defendant No.13 resisted the suit on presentation of a written statement controvert the statement made in the plaint. Defendant Nos. 18 and 19 jointly, also, presented a written statement. Stand taken by defendants are that they acquired title and possession over the suit property on the strength of Title deeds from Showkat Ali, the successive legal heir of Md Yasin Bepari. Defendants asserted their possession on the suit property over a period of 12 years.

6. Plaintiffs-opposite parties on 13-7-1979 presented an application for amendment of plaint.

7. Learned Subordinate Judge, Fifth Court, Dhaka on 14-11-1979 rejected the said application for amendment of the plaint taking the view that the original case put forward by plaintiffs would be totally lost if the proposed amendment was accepted.

8. Plaintiffs-opposite parties, thereafter, after a period of 14 years laid another application for amendment of plaint.

9. Learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 4 as the Trial Judge rejected the said application for amendment of plaint taking the view that a good number of new materials had been stated in the proposed amendment and in the event of allowing amendment the original plaint would virtually disappear. Learned Subordinate Judge also took into account the order dated 14-11-79 by which plaintiffs application for amendment of plaint stood rejected and plaintiffs did not take any proper steps against the said order of rejection.

10. Learned Subordinate Judge, thereafter fixed 15-5-1994 for per-emptory hearing. Plaintiffs, thereafter, on 15-5-1994 presented an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rehearing of the application for amendment of the plaint dated 26-10-1993 on recalling setting aside the order dated 27-3-1994 rejecting plaintiffs application for amendment of plaint.

11. Learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat by the order under challenge in Revision dated 19-10-1995 allowed the said application and reviewed order dated 27-3-1994 and allowed the amendment application of the plaintiffs dated 26-10-1993 in taking the view that for a resolution of the dispute the proposed amendment could be allowed.

12. Feeling dissatisfied the defendant Nos. 13 and 18 approached this Court in invoking Civil Revisional Jurisdiction on laying this petition under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule.

13. Basic grounds pressed into service in Civil Revision Petition are catalogued hereunder:

(i) Petition for amendment of the plaint under Order VI, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure was rejected twice on the ground that the nature and character of the suit could be totally changed and the original character of the plaint would be totally lost and learned Subordinate Judge committed an error in the decision.

(ii) Efficacious relief having been available to plaintiffs-opposite-parties learned Subordinate Judge could not modify and set aside earlier decision on the basis of an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

14. Statements contained in Civil Revision Petition have been controverter from the side of plaintiffs-opposite-parties by way of counter-affidavit. Statements made in counter-affidavit are that amendment in question is very much essential and the same is necessary to determine the real question in controversy between parties, in the suit regarding two genealogies. Further statement is that though the amendment application appears to be elaborate but plaintiffs only added a relief as to mesne profit is pursuance of subsequent developments and some statements made in the written statement by some defendants which are very much necessary for proper adjudication of the dispute in the suit.

15. Mr Shamsuddin Babul, with Mr Kanai Lal Shaha, learned Advocates appeared for defendants-petitioners. Plaintiffs-opposite parties are represented by Mr JN Deb, with Mr Ekramul Huq Tutul, learned Advocate.

16. In approaching and answering the question posed provisions contained in section 151 and Order VI, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure may profitably be noticed and considered.

17. Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure enshrines that nothing in the Code shall be deemed to limit or otherwise affect the inherent power of the Court to make such orders as may be necessary for the ends of justice or to prevent abuse of the process of the Court.

18. Section 151 of the Code does not formulate any new doctrine but only a legislative recognition of the well established doctrine and principle that every court has inherent power to act ex debitio justified and to do that real justice for the administration of which alone it exists. Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure can be invoked only to do complete justice between the parties and not to defeat ends of justice. It is well settled that this inherent power under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure cannot be invoked if other remedies are available to the party aggrieved.

19. Rule 17 of Order VI of the Code postulates that the Court may at any stage of the proceedings allow either party to alter or amend his pleadings in such manner and on such terms as may be just and all such amendments shall be made as may be necessary for the purpose of determining the real question in controversy between the parties.

20. The pre-requisite conditions to invoke the power of the Court for amendment of the pleading are that;

(i) Satisfaction of the Court that the proposed amendment is just and proper and;

(ii) that the amendment is necessary for the purpose of determining the real question in controversy between the parties. It is also well recognised that amendment cannot be allowed if the nature and character of the suit is changed or a valuable right accrued to the other side.

<u>20. Plaintiffs-opposite parties on 30-7-1979 presented an application for amendment of the plaint incorporating new facts and matters and the said amendment was even bigger that the plaint it itself. Certified copy of the amendment application covers 22 pages. Learned Subordinate Judge by order dated 14-11-1979 rejected the said application taking view that amendment petition is lengthy and burdened with new facts and matters and the original plaint would be lost in the event of acceptance of the proposed amendment. Plaintiffs-opposite parties did not move to Higher Court against the said order of rejection and appeared to have submitted to the said order of rejection recorded by learned Subordinate Judge. Plaintiffs-opposite parties after a period of long 14 years on 26-10-1993 presented application for amendment of the plaint. That amendment application was also a very big one. Learned Subordinate Judge by order dated 27-3-1994 rejected the said amendment application. Plaintiffs-opposite parties did not ventilate their grievance against the order of rejection before the Higher Court. Plaintiffs-Opposite Parties instead of moving before Higher Court on 15-5-1994 presented an application under the provision of section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for recording reasonable order on rehearing the amendment application dated 26-10-1993 on recalling or setting aside earlier order dated 27-3-1994. Learned Subordinate Judge by order under challenge in Revision allowed the said application on reviewing the order dated 27-3-1994. The order dated 27-3-1994 recording rejection of the amendment petition was a very much revisable order under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure and since a remedy in the Court was available to the plaintiffs-opposite-parties inherent power under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure could not be at all invoked and learned Subordinate Judge, thus, committed a substantial error of law in allowing the application presented under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure and, allowing the amendment application dated 26-10-1993.</u>

21. This takes me to another aspect of the matter. The application presented under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure was not a Review application and it was a plain and simple application under section 151 of the Code though grounds of Review had been also assigned in the said application. Even if the application under section 151 of the Code is couched as an application for Review but a Review of an order or Judgment can be only granted on specified grounds and conditions set out in Order XLII, rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure. A Review can be granted only on two grounds;

(i) discovery of new and important matter of evidence which after due diligence was not within the knowledge of the applicant seeking Review and

(ii) mistake or error apparent on the face of the record. Not mere error of law but error apparent on the face of the record is a ground of Review. There is a real distinction between "Erroneous decision" and an "Error apparent on the face of the record". Error apparent on the face of the record is an error which can be seen by a mere perusal of the record without reference to any other matter. A Review is by means an appeal in disguise whereby an erroneous decision is reheard and corrected but only lies on a patent error. The application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure even if couched as an application for Review, no ground of Review had been made out. In that view of the matter the learned Subordinate Judge committed a patent illegality in allowing the amendment application of the plaintiffs-opposite-party dated 26-10-1993 on reviewing the order dated 27-3-1994 recording rejection of amendment petition.

<u>22. It had already been stated that the amendment application incorporated so many new facts and matters. On perusal of the amendment application it appears that the complexion of the suit has been changed and the original character of the suit has been lost. Learned Subordinate Judge also in recording rejection of the two applications presented by plaintiffs-opposite parties took the view of mine. Turning now to the two amendment applications it appears that the statements made in the earlier amendment application dated 30-7-1979 and the subsequent amendment application dated 26-10-1993 may not be exactly similar but similarity of a great extent is manifested. In the event of rejection of the first amendment application there was no justification on the part of learned-Subordinate Judge to allow the second amendment application more so on reviewing the order dated 27-3-1994 recorded by him in refusing to amend the plaint.</u>

<u>23. Finality must attach to a decision rendered by a Judge and the decision recorded by the said Judge can be set aside or reversed not by the said Judge but by a Superior Judge. I took a similar view in deciding a case touching controversy relating to amendment of a plaint in Muzaffar Hossain vs Md Shahidullah and others 51 DLR 400.</u>

24. I have given my dispassionate consideration to all facts and circumstances of the case and also the legal aspect involved in the matter and I am of this considered view that the learned Subordinate Judge has committed a substantial error of law in allowing the application dated 26-10-1993 for amendment of plaint on reviewing the order dated 27-3-1994 recording rejection of the amendment petition and by this error a failure of justice has been occasioned.

25. Resultantly, the Rule arising out of the Civil Revision Petition got merit and the same, thus, succeeds. Rule is made absolute. The order under challenge, dated 19-10-1995 recorded by learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 298 of 1992 stands quashed.

26. Order of stay recorded by this Court on 13-12-1995 at the time of issuance of Ruse expired after four months of the said order dated 13-12-1995. Hence no order is required to be passed on stay matter.

No costs.

End.

vs.
Fabrication Foundry Engineering Works ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Gour Gopal Saha J: This Rule arises out of an order dated 14-6-1996 passed by the Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka in Money Execution Case No. 31 of 1995 staying all further proceedings of the Execution Case till the disposal of Title Suit No. 215 of 1992, subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 4 of 1995 filed by the opposite party.

2. Facts relevant for the purpose of disposal of the Rule, in short, are that the petitioner Bank as the plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 433 of 1984 against the opposite party before the Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 2, Dhaka for realisation of its outstanding dues and eventually obtained an ex-parte decree therein on 21-9-1987. Thereafter the defendant-opposite party filed Miscellaneous Case No. 58 of 1987 under Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the aforesaid ex parte decree but the said miscellaneous case was ultimately dismissed for default on 22-8-1988. The judgment-debtor opposite party thereafter filed another Miscellaneous Case No. 27 of 1988 for restoration of Miscellaneous Case No. 58 of 1987 but the same was also dismissed for default on 28-1-1989. Thereafter the judgment-debtor opposite party again filed Miscellaneous Case No. 22 of 1989, which was also dismissed for default on 24-5-1990. Subsequent thereto, the decree holder bank levied Execution Case No. 29 of 1989 before the Commercial Court, Dhaka for execution of the decree. In this execution case the judgment-debtor opposite party appeared and filed an application under Order XX rule 11(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for exemption of payment of interest of the detrital dues but the Execution Court rejected the said prayer. Thereafter, the opposite party filed Suit No. 215 of 1992 before the 4th Subordinate Judge; Dhaka for declaration that the decree obtained by the petitioner in Title Suit No. 433 of 1984 passed by the 2nd Commercial Court, Dhaka is void and inoperative. After filing the aforesaid Title Suit No. 215 of 1992 the opposite party filed an application for temporary injunction restraining the decree holder bank from proceeding with the aforesaid execution case. The learned Subordinate Judge by his impugned order dated 15-4-1996 allowed the aforesaid prayer of the opposite party and stayed all further proceedings of Title Execution Case No. 35 of 1995 (previously Title Execution Case No. 29 of 1989) till the disposal of Title Suit No. 4 of 1995 pending before the Subordinate Judge, Dhaka.

3. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid impugned order dated 16-2-1996 the decree holder bank moved this Court and obtained the Rule.

4. No one appears to support the Rule.

5. No one appears to oppose the Rule.

6. In view of the fact that the Rule arises out of an interlocutory order passed in an execution proceeding and all further proceedings of the execution case have remained stayed so long, we feel inclined to take it up for disposal on merit on the basis of the materials on record.

7. We have carefully gone through the impugned order and other materials on record. It is evident from the record that the judgment-debtor-opposite party tried its best to deprive the decree-holder bank of the fruit of the decree by adopting all dubious means and in the process it has been successful in forestalling the decree for well over a decade. The decree-holder bank is certainly at the receiving end. It is unfortunate that the learned Subordinate Judge stayed all further proceedings of the execution case by the impugned order, which is not only cryptic but is totally a non-speaking order.

<u>8. It must be remembered by all concerned that a decree passed by a competent Court has a sanctity in the eye of law and ordinarily it must be allowed to take its legal effect, unless there are convincing legal grounds to stay its operation. Filing of a subsequent suit by itself is no ground to stay further proceedings of an execution case. The judgment-debtor-plaintiff opposite party has placed nothing on record that may justify an order staying all further proceedings of the execution case till the disposal of his Title Suit No. 4 of 1995, filed 7 years of the passing of the impugned decree, after exhausting all legal processes to avoid it. The learned Subordinate Judge thus evidently erred in law in passing the impugned order in a most casual manner, without applying his judicial mind into the facts and circumstances of the case and the law bearing on the subject. It has, indeed, occasioned failure of justice. We, therefore, find sufficient ground to interfere with the impugned order.</u>

9. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka before whom Title Execution Case No. 31 of 1995 is pending for disposal, is hereby directed to dispose of the execution case most expeditiously, preferably within 6 (six) weeks from the date of receipt of this order.

Communicate the order at once to the learned Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No.1, Dhaka for his information and necessary action.

End.

parties:
Shahjahan Mia (Md) ----- Petitioner 
Vs.
Government of Bangladesh and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Farid Ahmed J : This Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned order No. 26 dated 12-2-2004 and order No. 40 dated 11-9-2005 passed by the respondent No. 2, Joint District Judge, 1st Court and Artha Rin Adalat, Faridpur in Artha Execution Case No. 30 of 2004 (previous Execution Case No. 18 of 2003 allowing the application of the respondent Bank to hand over the mortgaged property in favour of the Bank (Annexure-B and B2) respectively should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/ or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. The case of the petitioner is that the respondent No. 3 Islami Bank Bangladesh Limited, represented by Assistant Vice President, Islami Bank Bangladesh Ltd. Faridpur Branch, Faridpur as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 14 of 2002 in the Court of Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Faridpur for realisation of Taka 30,20,428 against the defendant-petitioner and two others. The said Title Suit No. 14 of 2002 was decreed ex parte on 10-3-2003 and accordingly, the preliminary decree was signed on 15-3-2003. The respondent No. 3 without filing any application for final decree as per mandatory provision of Order XXXIV, rule 5(3) of the Civil Procedure Code, filed the Decree Execution Case No. 18 of 2003 which was subsequently renumbered as Execution Case No. 30 of 2004 and the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Faridpur, most illegally started execution proceedings against the petitioner which is liable to be declared to have been proceeded without any lawful authority. Against the illegal proceeding of Execution Case No. 30 of 2004 the petitioner previously filed Writ Petition No. 3203 of 2005 which was heard and disposed of with a direction upon the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Faridpur, to dispose of the execution Case having regard to the provision of Order XXXIV, rule 4(1) of the Civil Procedure Code and section 5(3) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 but the Artha Rin Adalat without complying the direction of the Humble High Court Division and without considering the provision of law passed the impugned order for taking possession of the mortgaged property which is illegal, arbitrary and liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority.

3. The petitioner further stated that the Title Suit No. 14 of 2002 was a mortgage suit and the Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat passed a preliminary decree on 15-3-2003 and thereafter, without passing the final decree, has started the Execution Case No. 30 of 2004 against the petitioner which is not lawful.

4. The respondent bank on 13-6-2005 filed an application under section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 praying for an order to take possession of the mortgaged properties as per direction of the Court dated 12-2-2005 and the court by order dated 11-9-2005 allowed the said prayer without complying with the direction of this High Court Division.

5. The respondent No. 3 Bank has con-tested the suit by filing affidavit-in-opposition alleging that the petitioner was sanctioned an amount of Taka 25 lac on 1-8-1998. Subsequently, the loan amount was enhanced to Taka 33 lac for a period of 1 year. The petitioner failed to repay the said loan as per agreement. In such circumstances the Bank filed the aforesaid Title Suit No. 14 of 2002 for realization of Taka 30,20,428 as stood on 31-12-2001. The learned Court passed ex parte decree on 10-3-2003 and directed the petitioner to pay the said decretal amount within 60 days from the date. Thereafter the respondent No. 3 filed Execution Case No. 18 of 2003 which was subsequently renumbered as Execution Case No. 30 of 2004. On 3-11-2003 the judgment debt (petitioner) appeared in execution case by filing Vokalatnama and promised to re-pay the loan. The petitioner neither filed any appeal nor any application under section 19 of the Artha Rin Ain, 2003 for setting aside the ex parte decree. The petitioner also did not file any application before the Execution Court for drawing up final decree before proceeding with the execution case. The decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat is a simple money decree and that the provision of section 5(3) of the Artha Rin Ain, 2003 is applicable in case of mortgage suit for foreclosure but no final decree is required when a simple money decree is passed.

6. Mr AKM Shamsul Haque, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submitted that the Artha Rin Adalat passed a preliminary decree on 10-3-2003 and decree was signed on 15-3-2003 and thereafter the respondent bank without making any prayer for final decree started the execution case for realisation of the decretal amount which is contrary to the provision of section 5(3) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. Mr Shamsul Haque thereafter submitted that the petitioner previously filed Writ Petition No. 3203 of 2005 before this Court and this Court directed the Artha Rin Adalat to proceed with the execution case as per provision of Order XXXIV, rule 4(1) of the Civil Procedure Code and section 5(3) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, but the Artha Rin Adalat without complying with the direction of the High Court Division and without following the said provision of law illegally has been proceeding with the execution case which is illegal and liable to be declared void and without lawful authority. Mr Shamsul Haque further submitted that the order dated 11-9-2005 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat for delivery of possession of the mortgaged property in favour of the bank without following the provision of law and without drawing up final decree, is illegal, ultra virus and the same is liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority

7. Mr Md Golam Mostafa, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No. 3 Bank submitted that the Title Suit 14 of 2002 filed by the Bank was a simple suit for realization of money and the Court passed the money decree on 10-3-2003 and from the language of the said decree it would be evident that the said decree was a simple money decree and, as such, final decree is not required to be drawn up before selling the mortgaged property in auction. Mr Golam Mostafa also submitted that the decree was passed on 10-3-2003 and Execution Case No. 30 of 2004 was started when the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 came into force on 1-5-2003 and as per provision of section 5(4) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 no final decree is necessary before selling the mortgaged property in auction and the Court rightly passed the impugned order.

8. The case of the petitioner is, that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 14 of 2002 was a mortgaged suit and, as such, without drawing up final decree the proceeding of the execution case is not maintainable. Since, the Artha Rin Adalat has been proceeding with the execution case, the petitioner filed Writ Petition No. 3203 of 2005 before the High Court Division. This Court disposed of the Writ petition summarily on 15-5-2005 with a direction to the Artha Rin Adalat to dispose of the execution case as per provision of Order XXXIV, rule 4(1) of the Civil Procedure Code and section 5(3) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. Thereafter, the petitioner applied to the Artha Rin Adalat to follow the observation made by the High Court Division in proceeding with the execution case.

9. The petitioner has challenged two orders in this Writ petition. From order No. 26 dated 12-2-2005 it appears that the petitioner prayed for time to deposit the rest decrial amount and the decree holder filed an application under section 33(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat to issue a certificate vesting the mortgage property in the possession of the the bank. The Artha Rin Adalat allowed the application filed by the decree holder and rejected the application filed by the petitioner to allow him time to deposit the decretal amount. By order No. 40 dated 11-9-2005 the Court directed to issue writ for delivery of possession to deliver the possession of the mortgaged property in favour of the bank. From these two orders it does not appear that the petitioner made any prayer before the Executing Court for proceeding with the Execution case as per direction of the High Court Division passed in Writ Petition No. 3203 of 2005. Though the basis of whole argument of the petitioner is that the Artha Rin Adalat failed to comply with the direction of the High Court Division.

10. The learned Advocate for the respondent No. 3 has filed the photocopy of the certified copy of the ex parte decree passed in Title Suit No. 14 of 2002. From the said ex parte decree it appears that the decree was a simple money decree. The ordering portion of the said decree reads as under:

“প্রদত্ত কোর্ট ফি পর্যাপ্ত। অতএব আদেশ হইল যে, অত্র মোকদ্দমা ১-৩ নং বিবাদীর বিরুদ্ধে একতরফা সুত্রে খরচসহ ডিক্রি হইল এবং বাদী-ব্যাংক গত ৩১-১২-২০০১ ইং তারিখ পর্যন্ত বিবাদীদের নিকট হইতে ৩০,২০,৪২৮ (ত্রিশ লক্ষ বিশ হাজার চারশত আটাশ) টাকা এবং ১-১-২০০২ ইং হইতে বাদী ব্যাংকের সমুদয় পাওনা টাকা আদায় না হওয়া পর্যনত ১৫.১৫% হারে সমুদয় টাকা পাইতে হকদার। আগামী ১০-৫-২০০৩ ইং তারিখের মধ্যে বিবাদীগণ উক্ত অর্থ বাদী ব্যাংক বরাবর পরিশোধ করিতে ব্যর্থ হইলে বাদী ব্যাংক আরজির তপশীল বর্ণিত সম্পত্তি অত্র আাদালতের মাধ্যমে ক্রোকাবদ্ধ করতঃ উহা নিলামে বিক্রয় করিয়া বাদী ব্যাংকের সমুদয় পাওনা টাকা আদায় করিয়া লইতে পারিবে।”

11. The Title Suit No. 14 of 2002 was a suit for realization of outstanding dues and the court has passed the simple money decree. The suit was not registered as mortgage suit and the Court has not passed the preliminary decree. The decree passed in the aforesaid suit to be considered as a decree passed under sub-section 4 of section 5 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and as soon as the auction sale will be completed against mortgaged loan of immovable property the preliminary decree to be considered as final decree. Section 5(4) of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 reads as follows :

"(৮) The Transfer of Property Act, 1882 অথবা বর্তমানে প্রচলিত অন্য কোন আইনে বিপরীত যাহা কিছুই থাকুক না কেন, উপ-ধারা (৩) এর অধীন বন্ধকি মামলা ব্যতিরেকে, এই আইনের অধীন দায়েরকৃত কোন মামলায়, আদালত কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত ডিক্রি বাদী আর্থিক পক্ষে নিষ্ক্রিয় সমাপ্তির (Foreclosure) প্রাথমিক ডিক্রি হিসেবে গণ্য হইবে; এবং ঋণের বিপরীতে বাদীর অনুকুলে বন্ধকী স্থাবর সম্পত্তি ডিক্রির ধারাবাহিকতায় নিলাম বিক্রয় হওয়া মাত্রই উক্ত প্রাথমিক ডিক্রি চূড়ান্ত ডিক্রি হিসেবে গণ্য হইবে এবং বিক্রয় চূড়ান্ত ও ক্রয় বৈধ হিসেবে গন্য হইবে এবং অতঃপর উক্ত সম্পত্তি পুনরুদ্ধার করিবার কোনরুপ অধিকার (Right to redeem) বিবাদী দায়িকের থাকিবে না।”

<u>12. The aforesaid decree for realization of money was passed on 10-3-2003 as per provision of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990. The Execution Case No. 30 of 2004 was filed when the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 came into effect. From saving clause of section 60(3) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 it appears that the proceeding which were filed under the Artha Rin Ain 1990 but proceeded when the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 came into force, shall proceed as per provision of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 as far as it practical. So form this provision we find that the execution case has been proceeding in accordance with law. It does not appear from the impugned orders that the petitioner filed any application before the executing Court bringing allegation that the execution case has not been proceeded as per direction of the High Court Division passed in the aforesaid writ petition. We do not find any substance in this writ petition to interfere with the impugned order.</u>

In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to cost. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule on 26-9-2005 and the subsequent extension of the period of stay granted time to time is hereby vacated.

End.

parties:

Vs.
